message.content:
Explore the codebase at /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa and map out all AI-driven and automated code review workflows, CI/CD pipelines, and any human-in-the-loop processes. Be very thorough.

Specifically look for:
1. Any `.claude/` directory — agents, skills, hooks, CLAUDE.md, settings
2. CI/CD configs: `.github/workflows/`, `bitbucket-pipelines.yml`, `Jenkinsfile`, `.circleci/`, `azure-pipelines.yml`, etc.
3. Any PR templates or review templates: `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE*`, `docs/` review docs
4. Lint/format/test automation configs: `.eslintrc*`, `.prettierrc*`, `jest.config*`, `playwright.config*`
5. Any scripts related to code review or QA
6. `package.json` scripts that relate to review, lint, test, validate
7. Any agent definitions or AI workflow files

For each thing you find, note the file path and summarize what it does. The goal is to understand what automated/AI checks are already running as part of this project's review process, so we can determine what remains as human-in-the-loop responsibilities.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). content.content:
1	# Zimmermann - Salesforce PWA Kit (Production)
2	
3	> **STRICT RULE — TypeScript only inside `overrides/`.**
4	> Every file created or modified under `overrides/` **must** use `.ts` or `.tsx`.
5	> `.js` and `.jsx` files are not acceptable here, including theme files, stories, and config modules.
6	> Run `npx tsc --noEmit` before finishing any task that touches `overrides/`.
7	
8	Production storefront for www.zimmermann.com, a luxury Australian fashion brand. Must be robust and secure and SEO-friendly. See [.docs/architecture.md](.docs/architecture.md) for stack overview, overrides pattern, component organisation, and key paths.
9	
10	Tier classifications and protected-file lists live in [.claude/rules/](.claude/rules/) — loaded automatically per session. Custom slash commands for scaffolding and review live in [.claude/skills/](.claude/skills/).
11	
12	## Branch Rules
13	
14	**At session start, always run `git branch --show-current`.** If the output is `develop` or `main`, stop immediately — do not make any changes.
15	
16	| Branch | Branched from | Merges to | Allowed? | Notes |
17	|---|---|---|---|---|
18	| `feature/*` | `develop` | `develop` | ✅ Yes | Primary working context for new work |
19	| `fix/*` | `develop` | `develop` | ✅ Yes | Non-urgent bug fixes. Mechanically identical to `feature/*` — naming is for commit hygiene |
20	| `release/*` | `develop` | `main` **and** `develop` | ⚠️ Supervised | Plan-first + confirm-every-edit required. Code logic fixes must use a `fix/release-*` sub-branch |
21	| `fix/release-{version}-*` | the `release/*` branch | the `release/*` branch, then forward-merged to `develop` once the release ships | ✅ Yes | Only path for code logic fixes on a release. PR targets the release branch; SIT gate runs against the PR. Treated like `feature/*` on the sub-branch itself — the "Supervised" plan-first + confirm-every-edit rules apply only to direct edits on the `release/*` branch |
22	| `hotfix/*` | `main` | `main` **and** `develop` | ✅ Yes | Urgent production fixes only. Tier 1 rules still apply. Must be back-merged to `develop` to prevent drift |
23	| `develop` | — | — | ❌ Never | Human commits only |
24	| `main` | — | — | ❌ Never | Human commits only |
25	
26	> **On `release/*` or `hotfix/*` branches you MUST read [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) before any action.** It holds the supervised-edit rules (plan-first, confirm-every-edit, `fix/release-*` sub-branch flow) and the GitFlow back-merge rules that apply in addition to the Hard Rules below. On `feature/*` and `fix/*`, ignore it.
27	
28	## Hard Rules
29	
30	1. **Never operate on `develop` or `main`** branches.
31	2. **Never modify a Tier 1 file** without the developer explicitly naming it in the prompt and confirming owner approval — unless the verified-session exception in [Tier 1 Approval](#tier-1-approval--how-its-actually-enforced) applies. See [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md).
32	3. **Never modify `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`** — all design token changes go through the UI designer.
33	4. **Never modify `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, or `worker/main.js`.** These are absolute — the verified-session exception in [Tier 1 Approval](#tier-1-approval--how-its-actually-enforced) does not apply to them, regardless of approver status. `.github/workflows/` is Tier 1 CI/CD config and instead follows the standard Hard Rule #2 process (verified-session exception applies).
34	5. **Never refactor upward.** Fixing a bug in a component does not mean touching the hook or utility it calls.
35	6. **Never rename or move a shared hook or component.**
36	7. **Never add or remove packages** from `package.json` without integration team approval. When approved, always use `npm install` rather than editing `package.json` directly.
37	8. **Never modify test configuration files** (`vitest.config.*`, `playwright.config.*`, `.storybook/`, `tests/lighthouserc.js`).
38	9. **Never delete files** without being explicitly asked in the current prompt. You may propose deletion and let a human confirm.
39	10. **Never touch more than one protection tier** in a single change without stopping to confirm scope with the developer.
40	11. **Never assume a hook is safe to modify** because it has a simple name — check the frozenFiles list first.
41	12. **When requirements are unclear, ask one clarifying question at a time.** Do not proceed with assumptions and do not batch questions. Wait for the answer before asking the next question or writing any code.
42	13. **Never use `--dangerously-skip-permissions`** on `release/**`, `main`, or `develop`. This flag bypasses all edit confirmations and is only permitted in CI automation contexts, never in interactive developer sessions on shared or protected branches.
43	14. **Never reference code from a later sprint.** Check [.docs/memory/sprintScope.md](.docs/memory/sprintScope.md) before scoping any new work. If a task depends on a component, hook, or integration that belongs to a later sprint, stop and ask whether to build a placeholder or whether that sprint is already complete.
44	15. **Never create a git commit, push to remote, or open/close a PR** without the developer explicitly requesting it in the current prompt. Resuming from a session summary, a task list, or a "natural next step" is not an instruction to commit — wait for an explicit ask.
45	
46	## Tier 1 Approval — How It's Actually Enforced
47	
48	Claude Code's confirmation prompt before touching a Tier 1 file (Hard Rule #2) is a workflow
49	safeguard, not the security boundary — it can't be, since it only governs what Claude itself
50	does, not what any other tool or a direct `git push` can do. The real enforcement is server-side:
51	
52	- [CODEOWNERS](../CODEOWNERS) routes every Tier 1 path to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`, a
53	  real GitHub org team.
54	- Branch protection on `develop`/`main`/`release/**` requires an approving code-owner review
55	  before merge — this is the actual gate, enforced natively by GitHub with no Actions
56	  involvement, so it can't be affected by a broken or delayed CI run.
57	- `.github/workflows/protected-file-guard.yml`'s `tier1-guard` job posts a loud warning and an
58	  owner-contact-map on any PR touching a Tier 1 path. It is **not** a required status check —
59	  GitHub locked down cross-run check-run updates in Feb 2025, which made a "hard-fail until
60	  approved, then flip to pass on review" required check impossible to implement reliably (a
61	  fresh commit is needed to re-evaluate it, since a later review can't flip an earlier run's
62	  result). The CODEOWNERS-based review requirement above is the real, working block.
63	
64	Because the actual gate lives in GitHub, not in Claude's judgement, this file does not encode
65	personal names or email addresses as a bypass condition — a string in a shared, version-controlled
66	file is not an identity check; anyone (or any other Claude session) could satisfy it by typing it.
67	Instead, Claude may verify the real, authenticated identity behind the current session:
68	
69	- Before pausing to ask for Tier 1 confirmation, run `gh api user --jq .login`, then check
70	  `gh api orgs/ZimmermannAU/teams/tier-1-approvers/members --jq '.[].login'` (or check for `admin`
71	  via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/collaborators/<login>/permission`). If that GitHub
72	  login is a member of `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` or holds repo admin, Claude may proceed
73	  with the edit after stating which Tier 1 file is being touched and why — no separate
74	  confirmation message is required, since GitHub already recognises that account as an approver.
75	- If the authenticated login is **not** a member/admin, Claude must still stop per Hard Rule #2:
76	  name the file, and require the developer to secure an approving review from
77	  `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` before the PR can merge. CODEOWNERS auto-requests that review
78	  and branch protection blocks the merge without it, regardless of what `tier1-guard` reports.
79	- This check only ever reduces *how many times Claude pauses to ask*. It changes nothing about
80	  what GitHub will actually allow to merge — that's deliberate, so a compromised or careless
81	  Claude session can't grant itself write access to a frozen file.
82	
83	## Coding Task Workflow
84	
85	Every coding task follows these four steps in order. Do not skip ahead — pause at the marked points and wait for the user.
86	
87	1. **Clarify requirements.** Identify every gap, ambiguity, or contradiction in the request and the relevant `.docs/`. Confirm each one with the user before moving on — no assumptions. See Hard Rule #12: ask one question at a time.

# Zimmermann - Salesforce PWA Kit (Production)

> **STRICT RULE — TypeScript only inside `overrides/`.**
> Every file created or modified under `overrides/` **must** use `.ts` or `.tsx`.
> `.js` and `.jsx` files are not acceptable here, including theme files, stories, and config modules.
> Run `npx tsc --noEmit` before finishing any task that touches `overrides/`.

Production storefront for www.zimmermann.com, a luxury Australian fashion brand. Must be robust and secure and SEO-friendly. See [.docs/architecture.md](.docs/architecture.md) for stack overview, overrides pattern, component organisation, and key paths.

Tier classifications and protected-file lists live in [.claude/rules/](.claude/rules/) — loaded automatically per session. Custom slash commands for scaffolding and review live in [.claude/skills/](.claude/skills/).

## Branch Rules

**At session start, always run `git branch --show-current`.** If the output is `develop` or `main`, stop immediately — do not make any changes.

| Branch | Branched from | Merges to | Allowed? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `feature/*` | `develop` | `develop` | ✅ Yes | Primary working context for new work |
| `fix/*` | `develop` | `develop` | ✅ Yes | Non-urgent bug fixes. Mechanically identical to `feature/*` — naming is for commit hygiene |
| `release/*` | `develop` | `main` **and** `develop` | ⚠️ Supervised | Plan-first + confirm-every-edit required. Code logic fixes must use a `fix/release-*` sub-branch |
| `fix/release-{version}-*` | the `release/*` branch | the `release/*` branch, then forward-merged to `develop` once the release ships | ✅ Yes | Only path for code logic fixes on a release. PR targets the release branch; SIT gate runs against the PR. Treated like `feature/*` on the sub-branch itself — the "Supervised" plan-first + confirm-every-edit rules apply only to direct edits on the `release/*` branch |
| `hotfix/*` | `main` | `main` **and** `develop` | ✅ Yes | Urgent production fixes only. Tier 1 rules still apply. Must be back-merged to `develop` to prevent drift |
| `develop` | — | — | ❌ Never | Human commits only |
| `main` | — | — | ❌ Never | Human commits only |

> **On `release/*` or `hotfix/*` branches you MUST read [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) before any action.** It holds the supervised-edit rules (plan-first, confirm-every-edit, `fix/release-*` sub-branch flow) and the GitFlow back-merge rules that apply in addition to the Hard Rules below. On `feature/*` and `fix/*`, ignore it.

## Hard Rules

1. **Never operate on `develop` or `main`** branches.
2. **Never modify a Tier 1 file** without the developer explicitly naming it in the prompt and confirming owner approval — unless the verified-session exception in [Tier 1 Approval](#tier-1-approval--how-its-actually-enforced) applies. See [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md).
3. **Never modify `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`** — all design token changes go through the UI designer.
4. **Never modify `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, or `worker/main.js`.** These are absolute — the verified-session exception in [Tier 1 Approval](#tier-1-approval--how-its-actually-enforced) does not apply to them, regardless of approver status. `.github/workflows/` is Tier 1 CI/CD config and instead follows the standard Hard Rule #2 process (verified-session exception applies).
5. **Never refactor upward.** Fixing a bug in a component does not mean touching the hook or utility it calls.
6. **Never rename or move a shared hook or component.**
7. **Never add or remove packages** from `package.json` without integration team approval. When approved, always use `npm install` rather than editing `package.json` directly.
8. **Never modify test configuration files** (`vitest.config.*`, `playwright.config.*`, `.storybook/`, `tests/lighthouserc.js`).
9. **Never delete files** without being explicitly asked in the current prompt. You may propose deletion and let a human confirm.
10. **Never touch more than one protection tier** in a single change without stopping to confirm scope with the developer.
11. **Never assume a hook is safe to modify** because it has a simple name — check the frozenFiles list first.
12. **When requirements are unclear, ask one clarifying question at a time.** Do not proceed with assumptions and do not batch questions. Wait for the answer before asking the next question or writing any code.
13. **Never use `--dangerously-skip-permissions`** on `release/**`, `main`, or `develop`. This flag bypasses all edit confirmations and is only permitted in CI automation contexts, never in interactive developer sessions on shared or protected branches.
14. **Never reference code from a later sprint.** Check [.docs/memory/sprintScope.md](.docs/memory/sprintScope.md) before scoping any new work. If a task depends on a component, hook, or integration that belongs to a later sprint, stop and ask whether to build a placeholder or whether that sprint is already complete.
15. **Never create a git commit, push to remote, or open/close a PR** without the developer explicitly requesting it in the current prompt. Resuming from a session summary, a task list, or a "natural next step" is not an instruction to commit — wait for an explicit ask.

## Tier 1 Approval — How It's Actually Enforced

Claude Code's confirmation prompt before touching a Tier 1 file (Hard Rule #2) is a workflow
safeguard, not the security boundary — it can't be, since it only governs what Claude itself
does, not what any other tool or a direct `git push` can do. The real enforcement is server-side:

- [CODEOWNERS](../CODEOWNERS) routes every Tier 1 path to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`, a
  real GitHub org team.
- Branch protection on `develop`/`main`/`release/**` requires an approving code-owner review
  before merge — this is the actual gate, enforced natively by GitHub with no Actions
  involvement, so it can't be affected by a broken or delayed CI run.
- `.github/workflows/protected-file-guard.yml`'s `tier1-guard` job posts a loud warning and an
  owner-contact-map on any PR touching a Tier 1 path. It is **not** a required status check —
  GitHub locked down cross-run check-run updates in Feb 2025, which made a "hard-fail until
  approved, then flip to pass on review" required check impossible to implement reliably (a
  fresh commit is needed to re-evaluate it, since a later review can't flip an earlier run's
  result). The CODEOWNERS-based review requirement above is the real, working block.

Because the actual gate lives in GitHub, not in Claude's judgement, this file does not encode
personal names or email addresses as a bypass condition — a string in a shared, version-controlled
file is not an identity check; anyone (or any other Claude session) could satisfy it by typing it.

  login is a member of `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` or holds repo admin, Claude may proceed
  with the edit after stating which Tier 1 file is being touched and why — no separate
  confirmation message is required, since GitHub already recognises that account as an approver.
- If the authenticated login is **not** a member/admin, Claude must still stop per Hard Rule #2:
  name the file, and require the developer to secure an approving review from

  and branch protection blocks the merge without it, regardless of what `tier1-guard` reports.

#!/bin/bash
# PostToolUse hook: warn when a component in components/ or ui/ is edited
# and a paired *ContentfulDefinition.ts exists alongside it.
# Fires after Edit or Write tool calls.

set -euo pipefail

# Read the tool event JSON from stdin
input=$(cat)

# Extract file_path from tool_input
file_path=$(python3 -c "
import sys, json
try:
    d = json.load(sys.stdin)
    p = (d.get('tool_input') or {}).get('file_path', '')
    print(p)
except Exception:
    print('')
" <<< "$input" 2>/dev/null || true)

[[ -z "$file_path" ]] && exit 0

# Scope: only files inside a components/ or ui/ directory
if [[ ! "$file_path" =~ /components/|/ui/ ]]; then
  exit 0
fi

# Only .jsx and .tsx, skip the definition files themselves
if [[ ! "$file_path" =~ \.(jsx|tsx)$ ]] || [[ "$file_path" == *ContentfulDefinition* ]]; then
  exit 0
fi

# Look for a paired Contentful definition in the same directory
dir=$(dirname "$file_path")
base=$(basename "$file_path")
base="${base%.*}"
def_file="${dir}/${base}ContentfulDefinition.ts"

if [ -f "$def_file" ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "⚠️  Contentful definition exists for ${base}."
  echo "   If you changed props, run /contentful-drift-check to verify the definition is still in sync."
  echo "   Definition file: ${def_file}"
fi

exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Stop hook: ask Claude to reflect on the session and draft proposals
# for AGENTS.md, .docs/memory/*, and any other docs that may have drifted.
# Proposals are written to .docs/agents-proposals/ — NEVER edits docs directly.
set -euo pipefail

input=$(cat)

# Re-entry guard: if a Stop hook already ran this turn, do nothing.
active=$(echo "$input" | jq -r '.stop_hook_active // false')
[ "$active" = "true" ] && exit 0

branch=$(git branch --show-current 2>/dev/null || echo "no-branch")

# Skip only if nothing changed this session — otherwise always reflect,
# regardless of branch (develop/main/release included, just in case).
if [ -z "$(git status --porcelain 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

ts=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
proposal_path=".docs/agents-proposals/${ts}-${branch//\//-}.md"

jq -n --arg path "$proposal_path" '{
  decision: "block",
  reason: ("Before ending this session, reflect on what changed and draft any documentation updates. " +
    "Write a SINGLE proposal file to " + $path + " (create the directory if needed). " +
    "Do NOT edit AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .docs/memory/*, .docs/prd/*, or .claude/rules/* directly — those are Tier 1 / human-owned. " +
    "The proposal file should contain one section per doc you think needs updating, each with: " +
    "(1) the target file path, (2) a short rationale tied to something that actually happened this session, " +
    "(3) a concrete diff or before/after snippet. " +
    "Candidates to consider — only include the ones that genuinely changed:\n" +
    "  - AGENTS.md (rules, gotchas, unresolved deps)\n" +
    "  - .docs/architecture.md (stack/structural decisions, new integrations, key paths)\n" +
    "  - .docs/memory/projectState.md (phase, integration statuses, completed work)\n" +
    "  - .docs/memory/feedback.md (validated patterns, failed approaches, gotchas)\n" +
    "  - .docs/memory/references.md (new service URLs, dashboards, credentials locations)\n" +
    "  - .docs/memory/userProfile.md (newly-learned working-style preferences)\n" +
    "  - .docs/memory/sprintScope.md (sprint scope changes)\n" +
    "  - .claude/rules/frozenFiles.md or protectedFiles.md (tier reclassifications)\n" +
    "  - .claude/rules/conventions.md (new conventions discovered/agreed)\n" +
    "  - Any PRD under .docs/prd/ that contradicted what was actually built\n" +
    "If nothing meaningful changed, write a one-line file saying 'No doc updates proposed.' and stop. " +
    "Then end the session — do not start new work.")
}'

set -euo pipefail

#!/bin/bash
# PreToolUse hook: warn before editing a Tier 2 protected file.
# Non-blocking — exits 0. Emits owner and required action.
#
# Path conventions for this project's slim overrides layout:
#   overrides/app/... (not the upstream monorepo packages/template-retail-react-app/app/...)
#   .ts / .tsx inside overrides/ (both .js/.jsx and .ts/.tsx matched defensively)

set -euo pipefail

input=$(cat)

file_path=$(python3 -c "
import sys, json
try:
    d = json.load(sys.stdin)
    p = (d.get('tool_input') or {}).get('file_path', '')
    print(p)
except Exception:
    print('')
" <<< "$input" 2>/dev/null || true)

[[ -z "$file_path" ]] && exit 0

warn() {
  echo ""
  echo "⚠️  TIER 2 — $1"
  echo "   $2"
  echo "   Required: second developer review before this PR merges to develop."
}

# Global Shell — Both Squads
if [[ "$file_path" =~ /components/(header|footer|drawer-menu|list-menu|seo|_app|_app-config)/ ]] || \
   [[ "$file_path" =~ /app/routes\.(jsx|tsx)$ ]]; then
  warn "Global Shell" "Owner: Both Squads — notify both squad leads in #dev-team"
  exit 0
fi

# Shared Product Components — Squad B owns, notify Squad A
if [[ "$file_path" =~ /components/(product-tile|product-item|display-price|image-gallery|swatch-group|recommended-products)/ ]]; then
  warn "Shared Product Component" "Owner: Squad B — notify Squad A before merging"
  exit 0
fi

# Shared Commerce Components — Squad A owns, notify Squad B
if [[ "$file_path" =~ /components/(order-summary|promo-code|pickup-or-delivery)/ ]]; then
  warn "Shared Commerce Component" "Owner: Squad A — notify Squad B before merging"
  exit 0
fi

# Theme Component Styles — UI Designer
if [[ "$file_path" =~ /theme/components/project/ ]]; then
  warn "Theme Component Styles" "Owner: UI Designer — notify #design-system before changing"
  exit 0
fi

# Shared Hooks — Both Squads (5+ consumers)
if [[ "$file_path" =~ /hooks/use-(auth-modal|toast|modal-state|intersection-observer|currency|dnt-notification|app-origin|selected-store)\.(js|ts)$ ]]; then
  warn "Shared Hook (5+ consumers)" "Owner: Both Squads — signature changes require a team RFC"
  exit 0
fi

# Translations — Integration / SI Partner
if [[ "$file_path" =~ ^translations/ ]] || \
   [[ "$file_path" =~ /overrides/app/static/translations/ ]]; then
  warn "Translations" "Owner: Integration / SI Partner — coordinate with TransPerfect workflow"
  exit 0
fi

exit 0

=== code-quality ===
---
name: code-quality
description: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.
---

Audit code quality for the specified scope. Do not modify any files — this is a read-only
diagnostic. Produce a prioritised report with actionable fixes.

---

## Input

The user will provide one of:
- A file path or directory to audit
- No argument — default to files changed on the current branch: `git diff --name-only main`

If no argument is given, run: `git diff --name-only main` and audit those files.
Exclude test files (`*.test.ts`, `*.spec.ts`), stories (`*.stories.tsx`), and any registry files.

---

## Parallel execution

For audits covering more than 5 files, split into four independent checks and run them
as parallel agents simultaneously. Each agent receives only its own checklist — do not
bundle all checks into one agent.

- **Agent A — Naming & structure**
- **Agent B — Import analysis**
- **Agent C — TypeScript coverage**
- **Agent D — Test & story coverage**

For 5 files or fewer, run all checks sequentially in a single pass.

---

## Agent A — Naming & structure

Rules are defined once, split across [.claude/rules/conventions.md](../../rules/conventions.md)
(cross-cutting), [css.md](../../rules/css.md) (Chakra/styling), and
[components.md](../../rules/components.md) (components/hooks/Storybook) — read the relevant
ones first, then apply each rule to the files in scope. Do not re-list the rules here;
that's how the files drift apart.

Walk the file list and audit each file against the relevant section:

- Every file → conventions.md **General** section.
- Every file with JSX/Chakra props → css.md **Tokens** section (no hardcoded hex/px values).
- `.tsx` under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/` → components.md
  **Components** + **Composition** sections, plus conventions.md **File naming and folder
  structure**.
- `.ts` under `overrides/app/hooks/` → components.md **Hooks** section.
- `.ts` under `overrides/app/utils/` → conventions.md **Utilities** section.

For each violation, record `file:line` and which rule file + bullet failed — the section
anchor is enough (e.g. "components.md → Components → Props type placement").

---

## Agent B — Import analysis

For each file, read the import statements and check:

- No circular imports: if File A imports from File B, File B must not import from File A
  (check by reading the imported file's imports in turn — one level deep is sufficient).
- No imports from a higher tier without justification:
  - A component must not import directly from internal `commerce-sdk-react` source paths.
  - A page must not bypass its own hooks to call raw API functions.
- No imports from a later-sprint feature (reference `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` when present).
- No `../../../..` chains longer than 3 levels — flag for path alias review.

---

## Agent C — TypeScript coverage

Check each file against the relevant rule file:

- Every `.ts`/`.tsx` → [typescript.md](../../rules/typescript.md) in full (no `any` without
  justification, `type` vs `interface`, non-null assertions, discriminated unions, utility
  types, `import type`, `satisfies`, `readonly`, generic naming).
- Components → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Components** (props type name,
  placement, optional `?`, callback naming, JSDoc).
- Hooks → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Hooks** (typed params, explicit
  return type, JSDoc with `@returns`).

Then run `npx tsc --noEmit` **once** for the whole branch (not per file) and report any
errors. Cross-reference any new errors against the files in scope.

---

## Agent D — Test & story coverage

For each component file under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/`:
- A paired `*.stories.tsx` exists in the same directory (required by [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) > Testing).
- For logic-heavy components or hooks: a `*.test.ts` exists OR a `play` function exists in the story.
- If a test file exists, verify:
  - At least one test covers the primary render case.
  - At least one test covers a user interaction (click, input) if the component has interactive elements.
  - No tests use `toBeTruthy()` as the sole assertion — check for meaningful assertions.
- If a paired `.stories.tsx` is missing, flag as MISSING STORY (mandatory).
- If a logic-heavy file has neither a `.test.ts` nor a `play` function, flag as MISSING TEST.

For each utility file under `overrides/app/utils/`:
- **`.test.ts` required** when the utility has ≥1 conditional branch or performs ≥1
  transformation (currency, locale, mapping, parsing, etc.). Trivial re-exports and
  one-liners are exempt.
- If a test file exists, verify it covers both the happy path and at least one edge case
  (empty input, null, locale variation — whichever applies).

---

## Output format

Combine all agent results into a single prioritised report:

```
## Code Quality Report
**Scope:** [files audited]
**Branch:** [current branch]
**Date:** [today]

### 🔴 Must fix before PR merge
[Issues that would fail review or cause runtime errors — one line per issue with file:line]

### 🟡 Should fix in this PR
[Issues that affect maintainability or violate conventions — one line per issue with file:line]

### 🔵 Backlog (log, don't block)
[Minor style issues, missing test cases for edge cases — one line per issue]

### ✅ No issues found
[List checks that passed cleanly]

### Summary
X must-fix · Y should-fix · Z backlog items
```

Do not suggest refactors beyond the scope of the changed files.
Do not modify any files — report only.

=== pr-checklist ===
---
name: pr-checklist
description: Generate a PR description and merge checklist based on the files changed on the current branch. Pairs with /code-quality.
---

Generate a PR description and merge checklist based on the files changed in the current branch.

## Steps

1. **Run code quality check first.**
   Run `git diff --name-only develop` to get all changed files, then invoke the [/code-quality](../code-quality/SKILL.md) skill on those files. Include a summary of any must-fix issues at the top of the PR description. If must-fix issues are found, state them prominently and recommend resolving before opening the PR.

2. Run `git diff --name-only develop` to get all changed files.

3. For each changed file, determine its tier:
   - Tier 1: check [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md)
   - Tier 2: check [.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md](../../rules/protectedFiles.md)
   - Tier 3: check `.claude/rules/squadA.md` and `.claude/rules/squadB.md` *(if added)*
   - Tier 4: everything else

4. Check for cross-squad changes — files from both Squad A and Squad B territory in the same PR.

5. Output the following, copy-paste ready for a GitHub PR:

---

## PR Description

**Summary**
[2-3 bullets: what changed and why — be specific, not generic]

**Changed files**
| File | Tier | Owner | Reviewer required? |
|------|------|-------|--------------------|
[one row per file]

**Required actions before merging**
[Generated from tiers — examples:]
- Tier 1 change detected in [file] — confirm owner approval before merging
- Tier 2 change in [component] — a second developer must review this file specifically
- Cross-squad change — both squad leads must approve

**Notifications sent**
- [ ] [Squad/owner notified via correct channel]

**CodeRabbit pre-merge gates** (see `coderabbit.yaml` — these block merge in `error` mode)
- [ ] PR title follows Conventional Commits: `type(scope): description` (valid types: feat,
      fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, upstream-sync)
- [ ] Jira issue URL pasted into this PR description (not auto-detected from branch name —
      required for `issue_assessment` once the Jira Forge app is connected; recommended now)
- [ ] Any new/modified shared component (≥2 callers) or exported hook has JSDoc — see
      [components.md](../../rules/components.md) > Components / Hooks

**Test checklist**
- [ ] `npx tsc --noEmit` passes
- [ ] `npm run lint` passes
- [ ] `npm run test` passes (Vitest)
- [ ] Affected pages tested in local dev server (ask developer to run `npm start` — Claude must not start the dev server, see [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md))
- [ ] No regressions on golden paths for touched features
- [ ] No console errors
- [ ] WCAG 2.2 AA verified for any UI change — including `img alt`, `IconButton aria-label`,
      and `role` on any non-native clickable element (see components.md > Components)
- [ ] Any `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` wraps its value in a sanitizer (see conventions.md > General)
[Add specific items based on which pages/components changed]

---

Keep the output practical and tight. Flag any Tier 1 changes prominently at the top.

=== qa-generate ===
---
name: qa-generate
description: Generate a Gherkin .feature file and Playwright test spec from a Jira story. Human-in-the-lead — Lead QA validates the .feature before Playwright is generated. Use for any new storefront user journey that needs E2E test coverage.
---

QA test generation is a two-step, human-gated process. Do not generate the Playwright spec
until the `.feature` file has been explicitly confirmed by Lead QA.

> **Three testing layers in this project** (per [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md)):
> - Vitest — unit logic
> - Storybook `play` functions — component interactions
> - Playwright — E2E user journeys (this skill)
>
> The gherkin → Playwright workflow below is the **E2E layer only**. It does not replace
> the Vitest / Storybook layers — write all three where each applies.

> **Status:** the `e2e/` directory and Playwright harness must be in place before running this skill.
> If `e2e/` does not yet exist, stop and tell the developer the QA harness must land first.

---

## Phase 1 — Gather story details

Ask these questions one at a time. Wait for the answer before asking the next.

1. What is the Jira story key? (e.g. SFCC-142)
2. What is the story title?
3. What are the acceptance criteria? (paste them directly)
4. Which squad owns this story? (Squad A: checkout/cart/payments — Squad B: PDP/PLP/search/account)
5. Which sprint is this? (Check `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` — flag if the story references a later-sprint dependency)
6. Is this a P0 journey? (P0 = Digital SIT gate critical path: guest checkout, registered checkout, PDP variant selection, ATC, auth)

---

## Phase 2 — Draft the .feature file

Write the Gherkin file to:
`e2e/features/{area}/{JIRA-KEY}_{short-description}.feature`

Follow the standard in `e2e/features/README.md`:
- Tags: `@{JIRA-KEY} @{area}` — add `@p0` if confirmed in Phase 1
- Feature block with persona, goal, and value
- Background block for shared preconditions
- At least one happy path scenario and one failure/edge scenario
- Plain English only — no selectors, URLs, or implementation detail
- Under 150 lines — split by scenario group if longer

**Stop here. Do not generate the Playwright test yet.**

Present the draft and say:
> "This is the draft `.feature` file. Please share it with Lead QA for validation.
> When QA has approved or annotated it, reply with their feedback and I will proceed."

---

## Phase 3 — Apply QA annotations (if any)

If Lead QA returns annotations in this format:
```
# QA ANNOTATION: [correction]
```

Update the `.feature` file to reflect the correction. Confirm the change explicitly:
> "Updated [what changed]. No other changes made."

Repeat until Lead QA confirms the file is correct.

---

## Phase 4 — Generate the Playwright spec

Only proceed when Lead QA has confirmed the `.feature` file.

Write the Playwright test to:
- `e2e/tests/zimm/{area}/{JIRA-KEY}_{description}.spec.ts` — for standard tests
- `e2e/tests/zimm/{area}/{JIRA-KEY}_{description}.p0.spec.ts` — for P0 tests

Rules:
- Files are TypeScript (`.spec.ts`) — the TS-only convention applies to E2E too.
- Import Page Objects from `e2e/support/pages/` — never use raw selectors in the test file.
- Selector priority in POMs: accessible selectors (role + accessible name, label, text) > semantic HTML attributes (alt, title) > `data-testid` (only when no semantics apply). See [.claude/rules/testing.md](../../rules/testing.md).
- Import fixtures from `e2e/fixtures/` — never hardcode test data. Fixtures must be keyed by `SITE_ID` (Zimmermann has 7 storefronts across 11 active locales).
- Test description must match the Scenario name in the `.feature` file exactly.
- Use `waitForSelector` or `waitForResponse` — never `waitForTimeout`.
- Under 200 lines — extract shared logic to `e2e/support/helpers/` if needed.

---

## Phase 5 — Check for new Page Object needs

Read the generated test. If it references an element not yet in any Page Object:
- Propose the addition to the relevant `e2e/support/pages/*.ts` file.
- Do not create a new Page Object file without confirming the path first.
- Page Object files stay under 150 lines — propose a split if exceeded.

---

## Phase 6 — Summary

List every file created or modified:
- `.feature` file path
- `.spec.ts` file path
- Any Page Object additions

Then say:
> "The `.feature` file requires Lead QA sign-off before this test is considered complete.
> If QA annotates further changes, run `/qa-generate` again with the updated story key."

---

## Notes

- Never generate tests on `develop` or `main` — check `git branch --show-current` first.
- If the story references a component or hook from a later sprint (per `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md`),
  stop and flag it: the test may need to be deferred or the spec written with a placeholder.
- For Magento baseline regression tests, write to `e2e/features/regression/BASELINE-{area}-{behaviour}.feature`
  and note that these files use a `@baseline @regression` tag set, not a Jira key tag.

=== session-start ===
---
name: session-start
description: Run the mandatory session start ritual — reads tracking docs, runs branch + health checks, states current position. Use at the start of every coding session.
---

Run the mandatory session start ritual defined in [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md). Do this before writing any code.

## Steps (in order — do not skip any)

1. **Confirm branch** — run `git branch --show-current`. If the output is `develop` or `main`, stop immediately — no edits permitted (see [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) Hard Rule 1). If it matches `release/*` or `hotfix/*`, read [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](../../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) in full before proceeding — the supervised-edit and back-merge rules there apply on top of the Hard Rules.

2. **Read tracking docs** — read these in parallel:
   - [.docs/memory/projectState.md](../../../.docs/memory/projectState.md) — current phase, integration statuses (mock/live/not started), what's done and pending
   - [.docs/memory/sprintScope.md](../../../.docs/memory/sprintScope.md) — what exists this sprint, what is deferred. **Read before scoping any new work.**
   - [.docs/memory/feedback.md](../../../.docs/memory/feedback.md) — patterns to avoid or repeat
   - [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](../../../.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md) — current `@salesforce/retail-react-app` version and review state
   - [../session-notes.md](../session-notes.md) — lightweight, **gitignored, per-developer** carryover notes from your last local session (a Claude-writable staging area — see "Living Memory" below for how this differs from `.docs/memory/`). If it has pending items, surface them in step 4's "blockers or outstanding issues" and clear/promote each once resolved. It won't exist for a fresh clone or a teammate who hasn't used it — that's expected, skip silently.

3. **Health checks** — run when the helper exists:
   - `bash scripts/healthCheckAll.sh` — If the script does not exist yet, state that clearly and skip.

4. **State current position** — in plain language, say exactly:
   - Current branch
   - Current sprint / phase (from `projectState.md`)
   - The last completed task and the next task
   - Any blockers or outstanding issues

   Format: "Resuming from: [last completed task]. Next: [next task]. [Any blockers or health issues]."

5. **Confirm readiness** — ask if the user wants to proceed with the stated next task or redirect to something else.

Do not write any code until this ritual is complete and the user has confirmed direction.

---

## Living Memory — what belongs where

`.docs/memory/` is the project's persistent memory. Keep it current — update the relevant file whenever a session produces new information that belongs there.

**`.claude/session-notes.md` is different: a lightweight, Claude-writable, gitignored, per-developer staging area** (same pattern as `userProfile.md` below, but for tasks rather than profile info) for short-lived carryover items (e.g. "still need to do X next session") that haven't been promoted to `.docs/memory/` yet. It's **not** shared via git — each developer's notes stay local, so they never conflict or overwrite a teammate's. Unlike the files below, Claude may write to it directly. Use it for quick pending-item tracking; move anything durable and team-relevant into the right `.docs/memory/` file once it's confirmed, and clear the note.

| File | What belongs there | When to update |
|---|---|---|
| `architecture.md` | Stack decisions, overrides pattern, key paths, structural choices | A new integration is added, a structural decision is made, or a key path changes |
| `projectState.md` | Phase, integration statuses (mock/live/not started), what's done and pending, unresolved dependencies | Any integration goes live, a phase changes, a feature is completed, or a dependency is resolved |
| `feedback.md` | What worked, what failed, patterns to avoid or repeat | After discovering a gotcha, a failed approach, or a validated pattern |
| `references.md` | Service URLs, API keys, credentials, logins, dashboards | A new credential or service URL is introduced (system roles live in `architecture.md`) |
| `userProfile.md` | User's role, expertise, working style, preferences | User shares a preference or working-style detail that should persist |

**Rules:**
- Never leave a file with only its placeholder comment — populate it the moment you learn something that belongs there.
- **No duplication.** Every fact has exactly one home. Before writing something, check whether it already lives in another doc — if it does, reference that doc instead of copying. Applies across all `.md` files: `AGENTS.md`, memory files, and PRDs.
- **Conciseness.** Keep all `.md` instructions concise.

=== upstream-sync-review ===
---
name: upstream-sync-review
description: Review the release notes / changelog for a new @salesforce/retail-react-app version before bumping. Lightweight policy — see .docs/upstreamPolicy.md.
---

This is a **slim overrides project** on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` — not a framework fork.
The policy is **"read the changelog, bump opportunistically"** — see [.docs/upstreamPolicy.md](../../../.docs/upstreamPolicy.md).

This skill helps you review a candidate version bump before doing it.

---

## Input

Ask the developer:
> "What candidate `@salesforce/retail-react-app` version are we considering? Paste a link to the GitHub release notes or the version number."

If they give just a version (e.g. `10.1.0`), generate the release notes URL:
`https://github.com/SalesforceCommerceCloud/pwa-kit/releases/tag/v<X.Y.Z>`

---

## Step 1 — Capture current state

Read [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](../../../.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md). Note:
- Current version
- Reviewed-up-to version
- Any deferred items

---

## Step 2 — Read the release notes

Fetch the GitHub release notes for the candidate version (and any intermediate versions
between current and candidate). Summarise:
- Security fixes
- SCAPI / SDK breaking changes
- New configuration options
- Bug fixes that affect surfaces we override

The bump policy says: bump opportunistically only when a release contains **security** or
**SDK** changes that affect us. Otherwise stay put.

---

## Step 3 — Map changes to our override surface

For each notable change in the release notes, check whether we override the affected file
under `overrides/app/`. If yes, the upgrade may need a re-port of the override.

Quick check:
```bash
ls overrides/app/<area-from-release-notes>/ 2>/dev/null
```

For each override that may be affected, flag it as **Review** — the override must be
diffed against the new base file in `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` after the bump.

---

## Step 4 — Output a short recommendation

Produce a brief recommendation in this shape:

```markdown
## Upstream review: @salesforce/retail-react-app v<X.Y.Z>

**Current:** vA.B.C (per upstreamBaseline.md)
**Candidate:** vX.Y.Z
**Reviewed:** [today's date]

### Notable changes
- [bullet per relevant item from release notes]

### Overrides that may need re-porting
| Override path | Reason |
|---|---|
| overrides/app/... | [release-note item] |

### Recommendation
[BUMP / DEFER / WAIT FOR NEXT RELEASE] — with one-sentence reason.

### If bumping
- [ ] Update `package.json` and `package-lock.json` via `npm install @salesforce/retail-react-app@<X.Y.Z>`
- [ ] Re-diff each flagged override against the new base file
- [ ] Run `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`
- [ ] Update `.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md` (Current + Reviewed up to)
```

---

## Notes

- This skill does **not** modify any files — it produces a recommendation only.
- For Tier 1 files affected by the upgrade (`config/*`, `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `worker/main.js`), flag explicitly and require Integration lead approval before bumping.
- Do not run `npm install` yourself — the developer must approve and run it (see [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) Hard Rule 7).

=== generate-changelog ===
---
name: generate-changelog
description: Generate a release changelog from conventional commits and upstream baseline notes. Produces audience-specific outputs for the dev team, QA, product, and GitHub Release. Use before cutting a release branch or when preparing release notes.
---

Generate a structured release changelog. Ask clarifying questions one at a time,
then research in parallel, then produce the output. Do not write code.

---

## Phase 1 — Establish the release range

Ask these questions one at a time if not already provided:

1. What is the release version? (e.g. `v1.2.0`)
2. What is the base ref to compare from? (default: run `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` to find the last tag. If no tags exist yet, use the first commit.)
3. Is there anything specific that should be highlighted or excluded from the changelog?

---

## Phase 2 — Parallel research

Spawn three agents simultaneously. Each is self-contained.

**Agent A — Git log analysis**
Run: `git log [BASE_REF]..HEAD --pretty=format:"%h %s" --no-merges`
Parse each commit by conventional type:
- `feat` → Features
- `fix` → Bug fixes
- `perf` → Performance
- `refactor` → Refactors (include in technical changelog only)
- `test` → Test coverage (include in technical changelog only)
- `docs` → Documentation (include in technical changelog only)
- `build` / `ci` → Infrastructure (include in technical changelog only)
- `chore` → Maintenance (omit from product/QA changelogs unless `chore(deps)`)
- `upstream-sync` → Upstream sync (separate section)
- `style` → Omit from all changelogs

For each `feat` and `fix`, extract the scope (if present) and description.
Group commits under their type. Return the full categorised list.

433	---
434	name: upstream-sync-review
435	description: Review the release notes / changelog for a new @salesforce/retail-react-app version before bumping. Lightweight policy — see .docs/upstreamPolicy.md.
436	---
437	
438	This is a **slim overrides project** on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` — not a framework fork.
439	The policy is **"read the changelog, bump opportunistically"** — see [.docs/upstreamPolicy.md](../../../.docs/upstreamPolicy.md).
440	
441	This skill helps you review a candidate version bump before doing it.
442	
443	---

449

483	Quick check:

534	---
535	
536	Generate a structured release changelog. Ask clarifying questions one at a time,
537	then research in parallel, then produce the output. Do not write code.
538	
539	---
540	
541	## Phase 1 — Establish the release range
542	
543	Ask these questions one at a time if not already provided:
544

546	2. What is the base ref to compare from? (default: run `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` to find the last tag. If no tags exist yet, use the first commit.)
547	3. Is there anything specific that should be highlighted or excluded from the changelog?
548	
549	---
550	
551	## Phase 2 — Parallel research
552	
553	Spawn three agents simultaneously. Each is self-contained.
554	
555	**Agent A — Git log analysis**
556	Run: `git log [BASE_REF]..HEAD --pretty=format:"%h %s" --no-merges`
557	Parse each commit by conventional type:
558	- `feat` → Features
559	- `fix` → Bug fixes
560	- `perf` → Performance
561	- `refactor` → Refactors (include in technical changelog only)
562	- `test` → Test coverage (include in technical changelog only)
563	- `docs` → Documentation (include in technical changelog only)
564	- `build` / `ci` → Infrastructure (include in technical changelog only)
565	- `chore` → Maintenance (omit from product/QA changelogs unless `chore(deps)`)
566	- `upstream-sync` → Upstream sync (separate section)
567	- `style` → Omit from all changelogs
568	
569	For each `feat` and `fix`, extract the scope (if present) and description.
570	Group commits under their type. Return the full categorised list.
571	
572	**Agent B — Upstream baseline scan**
573	Read [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](../../../.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md).
574	Identify whether the `@salesforce/retail-react-app` version changed between BASE_REF and HEAD.
575	Use `git log [BASE_REF]..HEAD -- .docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md package.json` to find any bump.
576	Return: the version bump (if any) and a one-sentence summary.
577	
578	**Agent C — New components / hooks scan**
579	If `.claude/registry/` exists, run:
580	`git diff [BASE_REF]..HEAD -- .claude/registry/`
581	and parse for new entries in `components.md`, `hooks.md`, `utils.md`, `pages.md`.
582	Otherwise, fall back to:
583	`git log [BASE_REF]..HEAD --diff-filter=A --name-only -- 'overrides/app/components/**' 'overrides/app/hooks/**' 'overrides/app/pages/**' 'overrides/app/utils/**'`
584	Return: lists of new components, hooks, utils, and pages added in this release.
585	
586	Wait for all three agents before proceeding.
587	
588	---
589	
590	## Phase 3 — Sprint context
591	
592	Read `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` and [.docs/memory/projectState.md](../../../.docs/memory/projectState.md). Identify which sprint(s) were completed or progressed
593	in this release cycle. State it in one sentence for the product changelog.
594	
595	---
596	
597	## Phase 4 — Generate the changelog
598	
599	Produce the following four sections. Write them into a single file at:
600	`docs/releases/[TODAY]-[VERSION].md` (create the directory if it doesn't exist).
601	
602	---
603	
604	```markdown

606	
607	---
608

610

612	[From Agent C — list each new component and hook with its path under overrides/app/]
613	
614	### Features
615	[From Agent A feat commits — scope: description]
616	
617	### Bug fixes
618	[From Agent A fix commits — scope: description]
619	
620	### Performance
621	[From Agent A perf commits]
622	
623	### Upstream sync
624	[From Agent B — `@salesforce/retail-react-app` version bump (if any), what was reviewed]
625	
626	### Refactors & test coverage
627	[From Agent A refactor and test commits]
628	
629	### Dependencies & infrastructure
630	[From Agent A build, ci, chore(deps) commits]
631	
632	---
633	
634	## 🧪 QA Changelog (Test Team)
635	
636	### What changed that needs testing
637	[For each feat and fix commit, one bullet: what changed and which user journey to test.
638	Reference the relevant P0 test if one covers it. Flag any area where a P0 test does NOT exist.]
639	
640	### High-risk areas this release
641	[Any changes to: checkout flow, auth, pricing, cart, product display, navigation, consent (Didomi), international (Global-e).
642	State what specifically changed and the blast radius.]
643	
644	### Regression watch
645	[Any changes to shared components (Tier 2) or shared hooks. List the component and
646	all known consumers that should be spot-checked.]
647	
648	---
649	
650	## 📣 Product Changelog (Business / Stakeholders)
651	
652	### Sprint progress
653	[From Phase 3 — one sentence on sprint completion]
654	
655	### What's new
656	[feat commits only, in plain English, no technical detail. Group by user-facing feature area.]
657	
658	### What's fixed
659	[fix commits only, in plain English. Focus on customer-facing fixes only.]
660	
661	### What's coming next
662	[One sentence on the next sprint focus from .docs/memory/sprintScope.md]
663	
664	---
665	
666	## 🚀 GitHub Release Summary
667	
668	**[VERSION]** — [TODAY]
669	
670	[2–3 sentence summary suitable for the GitHub Release page. Highlights the biggest
671	feature additions and most significant fixes. Suitable for external visibility.]
672	
673	**Full changelog:** `docs/releases/[TODAY]-[VERSION].md`
674	**Release notes reviewed by:** [FILL IN]
675	```

685	Do not run the command — provide it for the developer to execute.

=== audit-tier ===
---
name: audit-tier
description: Identify the protection tier, owner, and import blast radius of a file or directory under overrides/. Use before editing anything you're unsure about.
---

Identify the protection tier and owner of a file or directory in this codebase.

The path to audit is: $ARGUMENTS

## What to output

**1. Tier**
- Tier 1 (Frozen) — must not be modified without explicit owner approval
- Tier 2 (Protected) — feature branch only, requires second-developer PR review
- Tier 3 (Squad-owned) — only the owning squad should be prompting Claude here
- Tier 4 (Feature-local) — freely editable on a feature branch

Check against:
- [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md) for Tier 1
- [.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md](../../rules/protectedFiles.md) for Tier 2
- `.claude/rules/squadA.md` and `.claude/rules/squadB.md` for Tier 3 *(if absent, infer from path: checkout/cart/payments = Squad A; PDP/PLP/search/account = Squad B)*

**2. Owner**
Design System / Integration / SI Partner / Squad A / Squad B / Both Squads

**3. Can Claude Code modify it?**
- Tier 1: No. Developer must name the file explicitly in the prompt AND confirm owner approval.
- Tier 2: Yes on a feature branch — second-developer PR review required before merging.
- Tier 3: Yes — but only the owning squad should be running Claude in this area.
- Tier 4: Yes, freely.

**4. Import blast radius**
Run this to check how many non-test, non-story files import it (from `overrides/app/` — the customisation surface):
```bash
grep -rl "$(basename "$ARGUMENTS" | sed 's/\.[tj]sx\?$//')" overrides/app --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx" \
  | grep -v '\.test\.' | grep -v '\.stories\.' | wc -l
```
If more than 5, flag it as **high blast radius** — a change here breaks many consumers.

**5. Next step**
Specific action for the developer — e.g.:
- "Message #design-system before asking Claude to touch this"
- "This is Tier 3 Squad A — if you're Squad B, message the Squad A Lead first"
- "This is Tier 4 — safe to include in your prompt with an explicit file path"

=== code-quality ===
---
name: code-quality
description: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.
---

Audit code quality for the specified scope. Do not modify any files — this is a read-only
diagnostic. Produce a prioritised report with actionable fixes.

---

## Input

The user will provide one of:
- A file path or directory to audit
- No argument — default to files changed on the current branch: `git diff --name-only main`

If no argument is given, run: `git diff --name-only main` and audit those files.
Exclude test files (`*.test.ts`, `*.spec.ts`), stories (`*.stories.tsx`), and any registry files.

---

## Parallel execution

For audits covering more than 5 files, split into four independent checks and run them
as parallel agents simultaneously. Each agent receives only its own checklist — do not
bundle all checks into one agent.

- **Agent A — Naming & structure**
- **Agent B — Import analysis**
- **Agent C — TypeScript coverage**
- **Agent D — Test & story coverage**

For 5 files or fewer, run all checks sequentially in a single pass.

---

## Agent A — Naming & structure

Rules are defined once, split across [.claude/rules/conventions.md](../../rules/conventions.md)
(cross-cutting), [css.md](../../rules/css.md) (Chakra/styling), and
[components.md](../../rules/components.md) (components/hooks/Storybook) — read the relevant
ones first, then apply each rule to the files in scope. Do not re-list the rules here;
that's how the files drift apart.

Walk the file list and audit each file against the relevant section:

- Every file → conventions.md **General** section.
- Every file with JSX/Chakra props → css.md **Tokens** section (no hardcoded hex/px values).
- `.tsx` under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/` → components.md
  **Components** + **Composition** sections, plus conventions.md **File naming and folder
  structure**.
- `.ts` under `overrides/app/hooks/` → components.md **Hooks** section.
- `.ts` under `overrides/app/utils/` → conventions.md **Utilities** section.

For each violation, record `file:line` and which rule file + bullet failed — the section
anchor is enough (e.g. "components.md → Components → Props type placement").

---

## Agent B — Import analysis

For each file, read the import statements and check:

- No circular imports: if File A imports from File B, File B must not import from File A
  (check by reading the imported file's imports in turn — one level deep is sufficient).
- No imports from a higher tier without justification:
  - A component must not import directly from internal `commerce-sdk-react` source paths.
  - A page must not bypass its own hooks to call raw API functions.
- No imports from a later-sprint feature (reference `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` when present).
- No `../../../..` chains longer than 3 levels — flag for path alias review.

---

## Agent C — TypeScript coverage

Check each file against the relevant rule file:

- Every `.ts`/`.tsx` → [typescript.md](../../rules/typescript.md) in full (no `any` without
  justification, `type` vs `interface`, non-null assertions, discriminated unions, utility
  types, `import type`, `satisfies`, `readonly`, generic naming).
- Components → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Components** (props type name,
  placement, optional `?`, callback naming, JSDoc).
- Hooks → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Hooks** (typed params, explicit
  return type, JSDoc with `@returns`).

Then run `npx tsc --noEmit` **once** for the whole branch (not per file) and report any
errors. Cross-reference any new errors against the files in scope.

---

## Agent D — Test & story coverage

For each component file under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/`:
- A paired `*.stories.tsx` exists in the same directory (required by [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) > Testing).
- For logic-heavy components or hooks: a `*.test.ts` exists OR a `play` function exists in the story.
- If a test file exists, verify:
  - At least one test covers the primary render case.
  - At least one test covers a user interaction (click, input) if the component has interactive elements.
  - No tests use `toBeTruthy()` as the sole assertion — check for meaningful assertions.
- If a paired `.stories.tsx` is missing, flag as MISSING STORY (mandatory).
- If a logic-heavy file has neither a `.test.ts` nor a `play` function, flag as MISSING TEST.

For each utility file under `overrides/app/utils/`:
- **`.test.ts` required** when the utility has ≥1 conditional branch or performs ≥1
  transformation (currency, locale, mapping, parsing, etc.). Trivial re-exports and
  one-liners are exempt.
- If a test file exists, verify it covers both the happy path and at least one edge case
  (empty input, null, locale variation — whichever applies).

---

## Output format

Combine all agent results into a single prioritised report:

```
## Code Quality Report
**Scope:** [files audited]
**Branch:** [current branch]
**Date:** [today]

### 🔴 Must fix before PR merge
[Issues that would fail review or cause runtime errors — one line per issue with file:line]

### 🟡 Should fix in this PR
[Issues that affect maintainability or violate conventions — one line per issue with file:line]

### 🔵 Backlog (log, don't block)
[Minor style issues, missing test cases for edge cases — one line per issue]

### ✅ No issues found
[List checks that passed cleanly]

### Summary
X must-fix · Y should-fix · Z backlog items
```

Do not suggest refactors beyond the scope of the changed files.
Do not modify any files — report only.

=== pr-checklist ===
---
name: pr-checklist
description: Generate a PR description and merge checklist based on the files changed on the current branch. Pairs with /code-quality.
---

Generate a PR description and merge checklist based on the files changed in the current branch.

## Steps

1. **Run code quality check first.**
   Run `git diff --name-only develop` to get all changed files, then invoke the [/code-quality](../code-quality/SKILL.md) skill on those files. Include a summary of any must-fix issues at the top of the PR description. If must-fix issues are found, state them prominently and recommend resolving before opening the PR.

2. Run `git diff --name-only develop` to get all changed files.

3. For each changed file, determine its tier:
   - Tier 1: check [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md)
   - Tier 2: check [.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md](../../rules/protectedFiles.md)
   - Tier 3: check `.claude/rules/squadA.md` and `.claude/rules/squadB.md` *(if added)*
   - Tier 4: everything else

4. Check for cross-squad changes — files from both Squad A and Squad B territory in the same PR.

5. Output the following, copy-paste ready for a GitHub PR:

---

## PR Description

**Summary**
[2-3 bullets: what changed and why — be specific, not generic]

**Changed files**
| File | Tier | Owner | Reviewer required? |
|------|------|-------|--------------------|
[one row per file]

**Required actions before merging**
[Generated from tiers — examples:]
- Tier 1 change detected in [file] — confirm owner approval before merging
- Tier 2 change in [component] — a second developer must review this file specifically
- Cross-squad change — both squad leads must approve

**Notifications sent**
- [ ] [Squad/owner notified via correct channel]

**CodeRabbit pre-merge gates** (see `coderabbit.yaml` — these block merge in `error` mode)
- [ ] PR title follows Conventional Commits: `type(scope): description` (valid types: feat,
      fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, upstream-sync)
- [ ] Jira issue URL pasted into this PR description (not auto-detected from branch name —
      required for `issue_assessment` once the Jira Forge app is connected; recommended now)
- [ ] Any new/modified shared component (≥2 callers) or exported hook has JSDoc — see
      [components.md](../../rules/components.md) > Components / Hooks

**Test checklist**
- [ ] `npx tsc --noEmit` passes
- [ ] `npm run lint` passes
- [ ] `npm run test` passes (Vitest)
- [ ] Affected pages tested in local dev server (ask developer to run `npm start` — Claude must not start the dev server, see [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md))
- [ ] No regressions on golden paths for touched features
- [ ] No console errors
- [ ] WCAG 2.2 AA verified for any UI change — including `img alt`, `IconButton aria-label`,
      and `role` on any non-native clickable element (see components.md > Components)
- [ ] Any `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` wraps its value in a sanitizer (see conventions.md > General)
[Add specific items based on which pages/components changed]

---

Keep the output practical and tight. Flag any Tier 1 changes prominently at the top.

=== qa-generate ===
---
name: qa-generate
description: Generate a Gherkin .feature file and Playwright test spec from a Jira story. Human-in-the-lead — Lead QA validates the .feature before Playwright is generated. Use for any new storefront user journey that needs E2E test coverage.
---

QA test generation is a two-step, human-gated process. Do not generate the Playwright spec
until the `.feature` file has been explicitly confirmed by Lead QA.

> **Three testing layers in this project** (per [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md)):
> - Vitest — unit logic
> - Storybook `play` functions — component interactions
> - Playwright — E2E user journeys (this skill)
>
> The gherkin → Playwright workflow below is the **E2E layer only**. It does not replace
> the Vitest / Storybook layers — write all three where each applies.

> **Status:** the `e2e/` directory and Playwright harness must be in place before running this skill.
> If `e2e/` does not yet exist, stop and tell the developer the QA harness must land first.

---

## Phase 1 — Gather story details

Ask these questions one at a time. Wait for the answer before asking the next.

1. What is the Jira story key? (e.g. SFCC-142)
2. What is the story title?
3. What are the acceptance criteria? (paste them directly)
4. Which squad owns this story? (Squad A: checkout/cart/payments — Squad B: PDP/PLP/search/account)
5. Which sprint is this? (Check `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` — flag if the story references a later-sprint dependency)
6. Is this a P0 journey? (P0 = Digital SIT gate critical path: guest checkout, registered checkout, PDP variant selection, ATC, auth)

---

## Phase 2 — Draft the .feature file

Write the Gherkin file to:
`e2e/features/{area}/{JIRA-KEY}_{short-description}.feature`

Follow the standard in `e2e/features/README.md`:
- Tags: `@{JIRA-KEY} @{area}` — add `@p0` if confirmed in Phase 1
- Feature block with persona, goal, and value
- Background block for shared preconditions
- At least one happy path scenario and one failure/edge scenario
- Plain English only — no selectors, URLs, or implementation detail
- Under 150 lines — split by scenario group if longer

**Stop here. Do not generate the Playwright test yet.**

Present the draft and say:
> "This is the draft `.feature` file. Please share it with Lead QA for validation.
> When QA has approved or annotated it, reply with their feedback and I will proceed."

---

## Phase 3 — Apply QA annotations (if any)

If Lead QA returns annotations in this format:

description: Run the mandatory session start ritual — reads tracking docs, runs branch + health checks, states current position. Use at the start of every coding session.
---

Run the mandatory session start ritual defined in [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md). Do this before writing any code.

## Steps (in order — do not skip any)

1. **Confirm branch** — run `git branch --show-current`. If the output is `develop` or `main`, stop immediately — no edits permitted (see [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) Hard Rule 1). If it matches `release/*` or `hotfix/*`, read [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](../../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) in full before proceeding — the supervised-edit and back-merge rules there apply on top of the Hard Rules.

2. **Read tracking docs** — read these in parallel:
   - [.docs/memory/projectState.md](../../../.docs/memory/projectState.md) — current phase, integration statuses (mock/live/not started), what's done and pending
   - [.docs/memory/sprintScope.md](../../../.docs/memory/sprintScope.md) — what exists this sprint, what is deferred. **Read before scoping any new work.**
   - [.docs/memory/feedback.md](../../../.docs/memory/feedback.md) — patterns to avoid or repeat
   - [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](../../../.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md) — current `@salesforce/retail-react-app` version and review state
   - [../session-notes.md](../session-notes.md) — lightweight, **gitignored, per-developer** carryover notes from your last local session (a Claude-writable staging area — see "Living Memory" below for how this differs from `.docs/memory/`). If it has pending items, surface them in step 4's "blockers or outstanding issues" and clear/promote each once resolved. It won't exist for a fresh clone or a teammate who hasn't used it — that's expected, skip silently.

3. **Health checks** — run when the helper exists:
   - `bash scripts/healthCheckAll.sh` — If the script does not exist yet, state that clearly and skip.

4. **State current position** — in plain language, say exactly:
   - Current branch
   - Current sprint / phase (from `projectState.md`)
   - The last completed task and the next task
   - Any blockers or outstanding issues

   Format: "Resuming from: [last completed task]. Next: [next task]. [Any blockers or health issues]."

5. **Confirm readiness** — ask if the user wants to proceed with the stated next task or redirect to something else.

Do not write any code until this ritual is complete and the user has confirmed direction.

---

## Living Memory — what belongs where

`.docs/memory/` is the project's persistent memory. Keep it current — update the relevant file whenever a session produces new information that belongs there.

**`.claude/session-notes.md` is different: a lightweight, Claude-writable, gitignored, per-developer staging area** (same pattern as `userProfile.md` below, but for tasks rather than profile info) for short-lived carryover items (e.g. "still need to do X next session") that haven't been promoted to `.docs/memory/` yet. It's **not** shared via git — each developer's notes stay local, so they never conflict or overwrite a teammate's. Unlike the files below, Claude may write to it directly. Use it for quick pending-item tracking; move anything durable and team-relevant into the right `.docs/memory/` file once it's confirmed, and clear the note.

| File | What belongs there | When to update |
|---|---|---|
| `architecture.md` | Stack decisions, overrides pattern, key paths, structural choices | A new integration is added, a structural decision is made, or a key path changes |
| `projectState.md` | Phase, integration statuses (mock/live/not started), what's done and pending, unresolved dependencies | Any integration goes live, a phase changes, a feature is completed, or a dependency is resolved |
| `feedback.md` | What worked, what failed, patterns to avoid or repeat | After discovering a gotcha, a failed approach, or a validated pattern |
| `references.md` | Service URLs, API keys, credentials, logins, dashboards | A new credential or service URL is introduced (system roles live in `architecture.md`) |
| `userProfile.md` | User's role, expertise, working style, preferences | User shares a preference or working-style detail that should persist |

**Rules:**
- Never leave a file with only its placeholder comment — populate it the moment you learn something that belongs there.
- **No duplication.** Every fact has exactly one home. Before writing something, check whether it already lives in another doc — if it does, reference that doc instead of copying. Applies across all `.md` files: `AGENTS.md`, memory files, and PRDs.
- **Conciseness.** Keep all `.md` instructions concise.

Generate a structured release changelog. Ask clarifying questions one at a time,
then research in parallel, then produce the output. Do not write code.

---

## Phase 1 — Establish the release range

Ask these questions one at a time if not already provided:

1. What is the release version? (e.g. `v1.2.0`)
2. What is the base ref to compare from? (default: run `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` to find the last tag. If no tags exist yet, use the first commit.)
3. Is there anything specific that should be highlighted or excluded from the changelog?

---

## Phase 2 — Parallel research

Spawn three agents simultaneously. Each is self-contained.

**Agent A — Git log analysis**
Run: `git log [BASE_REF]..HEAD --pretty=format:"%h %s" --no-merges`
Parse each commit by conventional type:
- `feat` → Features
- `fix` → Bug fixes
- `perf` → Performance
- `refactor` → Refactors (include in technical changelog only)
- `test` → Test coverage (include in technical changelog only)
- `docs` → Documentation (include in technical changelog only)
- `build` / `ci` → Infrastructure (include in technical changelog only)
- `chore` → Maintenance (omit from product/QA changelogs unless `chore(deps)`)
- `upstream-sync` → Upstream sync (separate section)
- `style` → Omit from all changelogs

For each `feat` and `fix`, extract the scope (if present) and description.
Group commits under their type. Return the full categorised list.

**Agent B — Upstream baseline scan**
Read [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](../../../.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md).
Identify whether the `@salesforce/retail-react-app` version changed between BASE_REF and HEAD.
Use `git log [BASE_REF]..HEAD -- .docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md package.json` to find any bump.
Return: the version bump (if any) and a one-sentence summary.

**Agent C — New components / hooks scan**
If `.claude/registry/` exists, run:
`git diff [BASE_REF]..HEAD -- .claude/registry/`
and parse for new entries in `components.md`, `hooks.md`, `utils.md`, `pages.md`.
Otherwise, fall back to:
`git log [BASE_REF]..HEAD --diff-filter=A --name-only -- 'overrides/app/components/**' 'overrides/app/hooks/**' 'overrides/app/pages/**' 'overrides/app/utils/**'`
Return: lists of new components, hooks, utils, and pages added in this release.

Wait for all three agents before proceeding.

Read `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` and [.docs/memory/projectState.md](../../../.docs/memory/projectState.md). Identify which sprint(s) were completed or progressed
in this release cycle. State it in one sentence for the product changelog.

Produce the following four sections. Write them into a single file at:
`docs/releases/[TODAY]-[VERSION].md` (create the directory if it doesn't exist).

```markdown
[From Agent C — list each new component and hook with its path under overrides/app/]

[From Agent A feat commits — scope: description]

[From Agent A fix commits — scope: description]

[From Agent A perf commits]

[From Agent A refactor and test commits]

[From Agent A build, ci, chore(deps) commits]

[For each feat and fix commit, one bullet: what changed and which user journey to test.
Reference the relevant P0 test if one covers it. Flag any area where a P0 test does NOT exist.]

### High-risk areas this release
[Any changes to: checkout flow, auth, pricing, cart, product display, navigation, consent (Didomi), international (Global-e).

## 📣 Product Changelog (Business / Stakeholders)

[From Phase 3 — one sentence on sprint completion]

### What's new

### What's fixed

## 🚀 GitHub Release Summary
```
