1	name: QA
2	
3	on:
4	  pull_request:
5	    branches:
6	      - develop
7	      - 'release/**'
8	
9	permissions:
10	  contents: read
11	
12	jobs:
13	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
14	  # Detect which expensive suites are actually relevant to this diff.
15	  # Unit tests always run (cheap, and the fastest signal). Storybook and
16	  # E2E are skipped — not omitted from the trigger, actually run and
17	  # reported as "skipped" — when nothing under their relevant paths
18	  # changed, so a PR touching only e.g. .github/workflows/ or AGENTS.md
19	  # doesn't pay for a browser-driven Storybook build or a full Playwright
20	  # run against the dev org. A job-level `if:` is used deliberately
21	  # instead of an `on.pull_request.paths` filter: GitHub treats a skipped
22	  # required check as passing, but a workflow that never triggers at all
23	  # leaves a required check stuck "Expected" forever and blocks merging.
24	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
25	  detect-changes:
26	    name: Detect relevant changes
27	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
28	    permissions:
29	      contents: read
30	    outputs:
31	      storybook: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.storybook_any_changed }}
32	      e2e: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.e2e_any_changed == 'true' || steps.deps.outputs.runtime_changed == 'true' }}
33	      vitest: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.vitest_any_changed == 'true' || steps.deps.outputs.runtime_changed == 'true' }}
34	    steps:
35	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
36	        with:
37	          fetch-depth: 0
38	
39	      - name: Get changed files
40	        id: changed
41	        uses: tj-actions/changed-files@2d756ea4c53f7f6b397767d8723b3a10a9f35bf2 # v44
42	        with:
43	          files_yaml: |
44	            storybook:
45	              - 'overrides/app/components/**'
46	              - 'overrides/app/pages/**'
47	              - 'overrides/app/hooks/**'
48	              - 'overrides/app/theme/**'
49	              - 'overrides/app/types/**'
50	              - '.storybook/**'
51	              - 'package.json'
52	              - 'package-lock.json'
53	            e2e:
54	              - 'overrides/**'
55	              - 'e2e/**'
56	              - 'config/**'
57	              - 'worker/**'
58	              - 'mobify.config.js'
59	              - 'playwright.config.*'
60	            vitest:
61	              - 'overrides/**'
62	              - 'vitest.config.*'
63	              - 'vitest.setup.ts'
64	              - 'tsconfig.json'
65	              - 'babel.config.js'
66	
67	      # package.json/package-lock.json deliberately aren't in the e2e/vitest path
68	      # lists above: those two suites care about *runtime* behaviour, and most
69	      # lockfile churn (a devDependency bump, a transitive-dep resync) can't
70	      # affect what ships to the browser. Only a change to package.json's own
71	      # "dependencies" block (a real runtime dependency) should force them to
72	      # run. Storybook keeps the blanket file-level check above — it's cheap
73	      # enough that being conservative there doesn't matter.
74	      - name: Check whether runtime dependencies changed
75	        id: deps
76	        run: |
77	          git fetch origin "${{ github.base_ref }}" --depth=1
78	          BASE_DEPS=$(git show "origin/${{ github.base_ref }}:package.json" | node -e "let d='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c);process.stdin.on('end',()=>console.log(JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(d).dependencies||{})))")
79	          HEAD_DEPS=$(node -e "console.log(JSON.stringify(require('./package.json').dependencies||{}))")
80	          if [ "$BASE_DEPS" != "$HEAD_DEPS" ]; then
81	            echo "runtime_changed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
82	          else
83	            echo "runtime_changed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
84	          fi
85	
86	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
87	  # Unit tests — runs on every PR to develop and release/**
88	  # This project uses Vitest (see package.json "test": "vitest run").
89	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
90	  unit-tests:
91	    name: Unit tests (Vitest)
92	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
93	    needs: detect-changes
94	    if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.vitest == 'true'
95	    steps:
96	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
97	
98	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
99	        with:
100	          node-version: '24'
101	          
102	          cache: 'npm'
103	
104	      - name: Install dependencies
105	        run: npm install --include=dev
106	
107	      - name: Run Vitest unit tests
108	        run: npm test
109	        env:
110	          CI: true
111	
112	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
113	  # Storybook interaction + a11y tests — runs on every PR to develop
114	  # and release/**. Exercises play() functions and @storybook/addon-a11y
115	  # component-level checks headless. Runs in parallel with unit-tests.
116	  # Runner: @storybook/test-runner (Playwright-based). Storybook is built
117	  # to storybook-static/, served by http-server, tested by test-storybook.
118	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
119	  storybook-test:
120	    name: Storybook interaction & a11y tests
121	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
122	    needs: detect-changes
123	    if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.storybook == 'true'
124	    steps:
125	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
126	
127	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
128	        with:
129	          node-version: '24'
130	          cache: 'npm'
131	
132	      - name: Install dependencies
133	        run: npm install --include=dev
134	
135	      - name: Install Playwright browsers
136	        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
137	
138	      - name: Build Storybook
139	        run: npm run build-storybook
140	
141	      - name: Run Storybook interaction and a11y tests
142	        run: |
143	          npx http-server storybook-static --port 6006 --silent &
144	          npx wait-on http://127.0.0.1:6006 --timeout 60000
145	          node_modules/.bin/test-storybook --ci --url http://127.0.0.1:6006
146	        env:
147	          CI: true
148	
149	      - name: Upload Storybook test results
150	        if: always()
151	        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
152	        with:
153	          name: storybook-test-results
154	          path: storybook-test-results/
155	          retention-days: 30
156	
157	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
158	  # Playwright E2E — every PR to develop and release/**.
159	  # Boots the PWA Kit dev server on localhost:3000 against the SFCC dev
160	  # org (real API, no mocks). Runs desktop Chromium + mobile Chrome.
161	  # BrowserStack cross-browser coverage is a separate job (release only).
162	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
163	  e2e-localhost:
164	    name: Playwright E2E (localhost)
165	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
166	    needs: [unit-tests, detect-changes]
167	    # unit-tests may now report "skipped" rather than "success" (see
168	    # detect-changes above) — GitHub's implicit success() over all `needs`
169	    # would otherwise treat a skipped unit-tests as blocking this job too.
170	    # always() bypasses that default so we can explicitly allow skipped.
171	    if: |
172	      always() &&
173	      needs.detect-changes.outputs.e2e == 'true' &&
174	      (needs.unit-tests.result == 'success' || needs.unit-tests.result == 'skipped')
175	    steps:
176	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
177	
178	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
179	        with:
180	          node-version: '24'
181	          cache: 'npm'
182	
183	      - name: Install dependencies
184	        run: npm install --include=dev
185	
186	      - name: Install Playwright browsers
187	        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
188	
189	      - name: Start dev server
190	        run: npm start &
191	        env:
192	          PWA_KIT_SLAS_CLIENT_SECRET: ${{ secrets.PWA_KIT_SLAS_CLIENT_SECRET }}
193	          ENVIRONMENT_NAME: dev
194	
195	      - name: Wait for dev server
196	        run: npx wait-on http://localhost:3000 --timeout 120000
197	
198	      - name: Run Playwright (desktop + mobile)
199	        run: npx playwright test --project=chromium --project=mobile-chrome
200	        env:
201	          SITE_ID: au
202	          PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL }}
203	          PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD }}
204	          E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU }}
205	          E2E_VARIANT_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_VARIANT_PRODUCT_SKU }}
206	          E2E_OOS_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_OOS_PRODUCT_SKU }}
207	          E2E_SALE_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_SALE_PRODUCT_SKU }}
208	          E2E_FIXTURE_ORDER_NUMBER: ${{ secrets.E2E_FIXTURE_ORDER_NUMBER }}
209	
210	      - name: Upload Playwright report
211	        if: always()
212	        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
213	        with:
214	          name: playwright-report-localhost

file.content:
name: QA

on:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - develop
      - 'release/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Detect which expensive suites are actually relevant to this diff.
  # Unit tests always run (cheap, and the fastest signal). Storybook and
  # E2E are skipped — not omitted from the trigger, actually run and
  # reported as "skipped" — when nothing under their relevant paths
  # changed, so a PR touching only e.g. .github/workflows/ or AGENTS.md
  # doesn't pay for a browser-driven Storybook build or a full Playwright
  # run against the dev org. A job-level `if:` is used deliberately
  # instead of an `on.pull_request.paths` filter: GitHub treats a skipped
  # required check as passing, but a workflow that never triggers at all
  # leaves a required check stuck "Expected" forever and blocks merging.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  detect-changes:
    name: Detect relevant changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      storybook: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.storybook_any_changed }}
      e2e: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.e2e_any_changed == 'true' || steps.deps.outputs.runtime_changed == 'true' }}
      vitest: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.vitest_any_changed == 'true' || steps.deps.outputs.runtime_changed == 'true' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Get changed files
        id: changed
        uses: tj-actions/changed-files@2d756ea4c53f7f6b397767d8723b3a10a9f35bf2 # v44
        with:
          files_yaml: |
            storybook:
              - 'overrides/app/components/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/**'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/**'
              - 'overrides/app/theme/**'
              - 'overrides/app/types/**'
              - '.storybook/**'
              - 'package.json'
              - 'package-lock.json'
            e2e:
              - 'overrides/**'
              - 'e2e/**'
              - 'config/**'
              - 'worker/**'
              - 'mobify.config.js'
              - 'playwright.config.*'
            vitest:
              - 'overrides/**'
              - 'vitest.config.*'
              - 'vitest.setup.ts'
              - 'tsconfig.json'
              - 'babel.config.js'

      # package.json/package-lock.json deliberately aren't in the e2e/vitest path
      # lists above: those two suites care about *runtime* behaviour, and most
      # lockfile churn (a devDependency bump, a transitive-dep resync) can't
      # affect what ships to the browser. Only a change to package.json's own
      # "dependencies" block (a real runtime dependency) should force them to
      # run. Storybook keeps the blanket file-level check above — it's cheap
      # enough that being conservative there doesn't matter.
      - name: Check whether runtime dependencies changed
        id: deps
        run: |
          git fetch origin "${{ github.base_ref }}" --depth=1
          BASE_DEPS=$(git show "origin/${{ github.base_ref }}:package.json" | node -e "let d='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c);process.stdin.on('end',()=>console.log(JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(d).dependencies||{})))")
          HEAD_DEPS=$(node -e "console.log(JSON.stringify(require('./package.json').dependencies||{}))")
          if [ "$BASE_DEPS" != "$HEAD_DEPS" ]; then
            echo "runtime_changed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "runtime_changed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Unit tests — runs on every PR to develop and release/**
  # This project uses Vitest (see package.json "test": "vitest run").
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  unit-tests:
    name: Unit tests (Vitest)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: detect-changes
    if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.vitest == 'true'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Run Vitest unit tests
        run: npm test
        env:
          CI: true

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Storybook interaction + a11y tests — runs on every PR to develop
  # and release/**. Exercises play() functions and @storybook/addon-a11y
  # component-level checks headless. Runs in parallel with unit-tests.
  # Runner: @storybook/test-runner (Playwright-based). Storybook is built
  # to storybook-static/, served by http-server, tested by test-storybook.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  storybook-test:
    name: Storybook interaction & a11y tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: detect-changes
    if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.storybook == 'true'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium

      - name: Build Storybook
        run: npm run build-storybook

      - name: Run Storybook interaction and a11y tests
        run: |
          npx http-server storybook-static --port 6006 --silent &
          npx wait-on http://127.0.0.1:6006 --timeout 60000
          node_modules/.bin/test-storybook --ci --url http://127.0.0.1:6006
        env:
          CI: true

      - name: Upload Storybook test results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: storybook-test-results
          path: storybook-test-results/
          retention-days: 30

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Playwright E2E — every PR to develop and release/**.
  # Boots the PWA Kit dev server on localhost:3000 against the SFCC dev
  # org (real API, no mocks). Runs desktop Chromium + mobile Chrome.
  # BrowserStack cross-browser coverage is a separate job (release only).
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  e2e-localhost:
    name: Playwright E2E (localhost)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [unit-tests, detect-changes]
    # unit-tests may now report "skipped" rather than "success" (see
    # detect-changes above) — GitHub's implicit success() over all `needs`
    # would otherwise treat a skipped unit-tests as blocking this job too.
    # always() bypasses that default so we can explicitly allow skipped.
    if: |
      always() &&
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.e2e == 'true' &&
      (needs.unit-tests.result == 'success' || needs.unit-tests.result == 'skipped')
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium

      - name: Start dev server
        run: npm start &
        env:
          PWA_KIT_SLAS_CLIENT_SECRET: ${{ secrets.PWA_KIT_SLAS_CLIENT_SECRET }}
          ENVIRONMENT_NAME: dev

      - name: Wait for dev server
        run: npx wait-on http://localhost:3000 --timeout 120000

      - name: Run Playwright (desktop + mobile)
        run: npx playwright test --project=chromium --project=mobile-chrome
        env:
          SITE_ID: au
          PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL }}
          PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD }}
          E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU }}
          E2E_VARIANT_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_VARIANT_PRODUCT_SKU }}
          E2E_OOS_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_OOS_PRODUCT_SKU }}
          E2E_SALE_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_SALE_PRODUCT_SKU }}
          E2E_FIXTURE_ORDER_NUMBER: ${{ secrets.E2E_FIXTURE_ORDER_NUMBER }}

      - name: Upload Playwright report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: playwright-report-localhost
          path: playwright-report/
          retention-days: 30

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # BrowserStack cross-browser regression — release PRs only.
  # Complements the SIT gate (digital-sit.yml) with multi-browser
  # coverage. The e2e/tests/zimm/ suite and browserstack-node-sdk wiring
  # are in place — this job only runs on release/** PRs.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  e2e-browserstack:
    name: Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [unit-tests, detect-changes]
    # Same always()/skipped handling as e2e-localhost above.
    if: |
      always() &&
      contains(github.base_ref, 'release/') &&
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.e2e == 'true' &&
      (needs.unit-tests.result == 'success' || needs.unit-tests.result == 'skipped')

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Run Zimmermann e2e on BrowserStack
        run: npx browserstack-node-sdk playwright test e2e/tests/zimm
        env:
          BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME }}
          BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY }}
          SPRINT_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}
          RETAIL_APP_HOME: ${{ secrets.RETAIL_APP_HOME_SIT }}
          PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL }}
          PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD }}
          E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU }}
          E2E_VARIANT_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_VARIANT_PRODUCT_SKU }}
          E2E_OOS_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_OOS_PRODUCT_SKU }}
          E2E_SALE_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_SALE_PRODUCT_SKU }}
          E2E_FIXTURE_ORDER_NUMBER: ${{ secrets.E2E_FIXTURE_ORDER_NUMBER }}
          SITE_ID: au  # Default — parameterise for multi-region runs

21	        id: sweep

26	          # Per Zimmermann convention every UI component must have a paired .stories.tsx;
27	          # a .test.ts(x) is required for logic-heavy components but not for every leaf.
28	          # Flag any component file that lacks BOTH a story and a test.
29	          while IFS= read -r file; do
30	            base="${file%.*}"
31	            dir=$(dirname "$file")
32	            name=$(basename "$base")

35	            for t in "${base}.test.ts" "${base}.test.tsx" "${base}.stories.tsx" \

37	                     "${dir}/index.test.ts" "${dir}/index.test.tsx" "${dir}/index.stories.tsx"; do
38	              [[ -f "$t" ]] && found=true && break
39	            done
40	            $found || missing+=("$file")
41	          done < <(find overrides/app/components \
42	            \( -name "index.tsx" -o -name "index.ts" \) \

44	
45	          # Hooks: look for use-*.ts (override convention keeps kebab-case) and useFoo.ts
46	          # (Zimmermann camelCase convention) without a paired test file.
47	          while IFS= read -r file; do
48	            base="${file%.*}"
49	            found=false
50	            for t in "${base}.test.ts" "${base}.test.tsx"; do
51	              [[ -f "$t" ]] && found=true && break
52	            done
53	            $found || missing+=("$file")
54	          done < <(find overrides/app/hooks \
55	            \( -name "use-*.ts" -o -name "use[A-Z]*.ts" \) \
56	            ! -path "*/node_modules/*" 2>/dev/null | sort)
57	
58	          # Write results
59	          COUNT=${#missing[@]}
60	          echo "count=$COUNT" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
61	
62	          if [[ $COUNT -gt 0 ]]; then
63	            printf '%s\n' "${missing[@]}" > /tmp/missing-tests.txt
64	            echo "has_missing=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
65	          else
66	            echo "has_missing=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
67	          fi
68	
69	      - name: Check for existing open quality-sweep issue
70	        id: existing
71	        if: steps.sweep.outputs.has_missing == 'true'
72	        env:
73	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
74	        run: |
75	          NUM=$(gh issue list \
76	            --label "quality-sweep" \
77	            --state open \
78	            --json number \
79	            --jq '.[0].number // empty')
80	          echo "number=$NUM" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
81	
82	      - name: Create or update quality sweep issue
83	        if: steps.sweep.outputs.has_missing == 'true'
84	        env:
85	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
86	        run: |
87	          COUNT="${{ steps.sweep.outputs.count }}"
88	          DATE=$(date +%Y-%m-%d)

91	          CHECKLIST=""
92	          while IFS= read -r file; do

96	
97	          BODY=$(cat <<EOF
98	          ## Weekly Quality Sweep — $DATE
99	
100	          **$COUNT** component/hook file(s) are missing a paired test or story.
101	
102	          ### Files without tests or stories
103	
104	          $CHECKLIST
105	
106	          ### How to fix
107	
108	          - Components: add a \`.stories.tsx\` (required) and a \`.test.ts(x)\` if the component has logic worth testing — see AGENTS.md > Testing.
109	          - Hooks: add a paired \`.test.ts\`.

112	
113	          ---
114	          *Updated automatically by the weekly-agents workflow.*
115	          *Close this issue once all items are checked off.*
116	          EOF
117	          )
118	
119	          EXISTING="${{ steps.existing.outputs.number }}"
120	          if [[ -n "$EXISTING" ]]; then
121	            gh issue edit "$EXISTING" \
122	              --title "Quality sweep: $COUNT files missing tests/stories ($DATE)" \
123	              --body "$BODY"
124	            echo "Updated existing issue #$EXISTING"
125	          else
126	            gh issue create \
127	              --title "Quality sweep: $COUNT files missing tests/stories ($DATE)" \
128	              --label "quality-sweep,tech-debt" \
129	              --body "$BODY"
130	          fi

133	        if: steps.sweep.outputs.has_missing == 'false'

159	          issues=()
160	
161	          # Find all ContentfulDefinition.ts files under overrides/app/components/
162	          while IFS= read -r def_file; do
163	            dir=$(dirname "$def_file")

200	
201	          EXISTING=$(gh issue list \
202	            --label "contentful-drift" \
203	            --state open \
204	            --json number \
205	            --jq '.[0].number // empty')
206	
207	          BODY=$(cat <<EOF
208	          ## Contentful Drift Audit — $DATE
209	
210	          **$COUNT** structural issue(s) found in Contentful component definitions.
211	
212	          ### Issues found
213	
214	          $ITEMS
215	
216	          ### Next steps
217	
218	          Run \`/contentful-drift-check\` in a Claude Code session for a detailed
219	          prop-level comparison between component interfaces and their Contentful definitions.
220	
221	          ---
222	          *Note: This automated check detects structural issues (orphaned files, missing pairs).*
223	          *Prop-level drift requires running \`/contentful-drift-check\` manually.*
224	          *Updated automatically by the weekly-agents workflow.*
225	          EOF
226	          )
227	
228	          if [[ -n "$EXISTING" ]]; then
229	            gh issue edit "$EXISTING" \
230	              --title "Contentful drift audit: $COUNT issue(s) found ($DATE)" \
231	              --body "$BODY"
232	          else
233	            gh issue create \
234	              --title "Contentful drift audit: $COUNT issue(s) found ($DATE)" \
235	              --label "contentful-drift,needs-review" \
236	              --body "$BODY"
237	          fi
238	
239	      - name: No Contentful drift issues
240	        if: steps.audit.outputs.has_issues == 'false'
241	        env:
242	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
243	        run: |
244	          echo "✅ No structural Contentful definition issues found."
245	          EXISTING=$(gh issue list \
246	            --label "contentful-drift" \
247	            --state open \
248	            --json number \
249	            --jq '.[0].number // empty')
250	          if [[ -n "$EXISTING" ]]; then
251	            gh issue close "$EXISTING" \
252	              --comment "✅ No structural issues found this week. Closing automatically."
253	          fi
254	
255	  changelog-reminder:
256	    name: Changelog reminder for open release PRs
257	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
258	    steps:
259	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
260	
261	      - name: Check for open PRs targeting release branches without a changelog entry
262	        env:
263	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
264	        run: |
265	          # Find open PRs targeting release/**
266	          PRS=$(gh pr list \
267	            --base "release" \
268	            --state open \
269	            --json number,title,headRefName \
270	            --jq '.[] | "\(.number) \(.title)"' 2>/dev/null || true)
271	
272	          if [[ -z "$PRS" ]]; then
273	            echo "No open PRs targeting release branches."
274	            exit 0
275	          fi
276	
277	          while IFS= read -r pr; do
278	            PR_NUM=$(echo "$pr" | cut -d' ' -f1)
279	            # Check if the PR already has a changelog comment
280	            HAS_CHANGELOG=$(gh pr view "$PR_NUM" --json comments \
281	              --jq '[.comments[].body | select(contains("generate-changelog"))] | length')
282	            if [[ "$HAS_CHANGELOG" -eq 0 ]]; then
283	              gh pr comment "$PR_NUM" --body "$(cat <<EOF
284	          ### 📋 Changelog reminder
285	
286	          This PR targets a release branch. Before merging, run:
287	
288	          \`\`\`
289	          /generate-changelog
290	          \`\`\`
291	
292	          This will produce audience-specific release notes for the dev team, QA, product, and GitHub Release.
293	          Commit the output to \`docs/releases/\` as part of this PR.
294	          EOF
295	          )"
296	            fi
297	          done <<< "$PRS"

jobs:
  quality-sweep:
    name: Quality sweep — missing tests or stories
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Find components and hooks without paired tests/stories
        id: sweep
        run: |
          missing=()

          # Components under overrides/app/components/ — TypeScript only per AGENTS.md.
          # Per Zimmermann convention every UI component must have a paired .stories.tsx;
          # a .test.ts(x) is required for logic-heavy components but not for every leaf.
          # Flag any component file that lacks BOTH a story and a test.
          while IFS= read -r file; do
            base="${file%.*}"
            dir=$(dirname "$file")
            name=$(basename "$base")
            found=false
            # Check for paired test or story (same basename or co-located in the same folder)
            for t in "${base}.test.ts" "${base}.test.tsx" "${base}.stories.tsx" \
                     "${dir}/${name}.test.ts" "${dir}/${name}.test.tsx" "${dir}/${name}.stories.tsx" \
                     "${dir}/index.test.ts" "${dir}/index.test.tsx" "${dir}/index.stories.tsx"; do
              [[ -f "$t" ]] && found=true && break
            done
            $found || missing+=("$file")
          done < <(find overrides/app/components \
            \( -name "index.tsx" -o -name "index.ts" \) \
            ! -path "*/node_modules/*" 2>/dev/null | sort)

          # Hooks: look for use-*.ts (override convention keeps kebab-case) and useFoo.ts
          # (Zimmermann camelCase convention) without a paired test file.
          while IFS= read -r file; do
            base="${file%.*}"
            found=false
            for t in "${base}.test.ts" "${base}.test.tsx"; do
              [[ -f "$t" ]] && found=true && break
            done
            $found || missing+=("$file")
          done < <(find overrides/app/hooks \
            \( -name "use-*.ts" -o -name "use[A-Z]*.ts" \) \
            ! -path "*/node_modules/*" 2>/dev/null | sort)

          # Write results
          COUNT=${#missing[@]}
          echo "count=$COUNT" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

          if [[ $COUNT -gt 0 ]]; then
            printf '%s\n' "${missing[@]}" > /tmp/missing-tests.txt
            echo "has_missing=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          else
            echo "has_missing=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi

      - name: Check for existing open quality-sweep issue
        id: existing
        if: steps.sweep.outputs.has_missing == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          NUM=$(gh issue list \
            --label "quality-sweep" \
            --state open \
            --json number \
            --jq '.[0].number // empty')
          echo "number=$NUM" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Create or update quality sweep issue
        if: steps.sweep.outputs.has_missing == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          COUNT="${{ steps.sweep.outputs.count }}"
          DATE=$(date +%Y-%m-%d)

          # Format the missing files list as a checklist
          CHECKLIST=""
          while IFS= read -r file; do
            short="${file#overrides/}"
            CHECKLIST="${CHECKLIST}- [ ] \`${short}\`"$'\n'
          done < /tmp/missing-tests.txt

          BODY=$(cat <<EOF
          ## Weekly Quality Sweep — $DATE

          **$COUNT** component/hook file(s) are missing a paired test or story.

          ### Files without tests or stories

          $CHECKLIST

          ### How to fix

          - Components: add a \`.stories.tsx\` (required) and a \`.test.ts(x)\` if the component has logic worth testing — see AGENTS.md > Testing.
          - Hooks: add a paired \`.test.ts\`.

          Run \`/code-quality\` in a Claude Code session to get specific test case suggestions.

          ---
          *Updated automatically by the weekly-agents workflow.*
          *Close this issue once all items are checked off.*
          EOF
          )

          EXISTING="${{ steps.existing.outputs.number }}"
          if [[ -n "$EXISTING" ]]; then
            gh issue edit "$EXISTING" \
              --title "Quality sweep: $COUNT files missing tests/stories ($DATE)" \
              --body "$BODY"
            echo "Updated existing issue #$EXISTING"
          else
            gh issue create \
              --title "Quality sweep: $COUNT files missing tests/stories ($DATE)" \
              --label "quality-sweep,tech-debt" \
              --body "$BODY"
          fi

      - name: All tests/stories present
        if: steps.sweep.outputs.has_missing == 'false'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          echo "✅ All components and hooks have paired tests or stories."

          # Close any open quality-sweep issue if everything is now covered
          EXISTING=$(gh issue list \
            --label "quality-sweep" \
            --state open \
            --json number \
            --jq '.[0].number // empty')
          if [[ -n "$EXISTING" ]]; then
            gh issue close "$EXISTING" \
              --comment "✅ All files now have test/story coverage. Closing automatically."
          fi

  contentful-drift-audit:
    name: Contentful drift audit
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Check for definition files without paired components
        id: audit
        run: |
          issues=()

          # Find all ContentfulDefinition.ts files under overrides/app/components/
          while IFS= read -r def_file; do
            dir=$(dirname "$def_file")
            base=$(basename "$def_file" ContentfulDefinition.ts)

            # Check for a paired component file
            found=false
            for ext in tsx ts; do
              [[ -f "${dir}/${base}.${ext}" ]] && found=true && break
              [[ -f "${dir}/index.${ext}" ]] && found=true && break
            done

            $found || issues+=("Orphaned definition (no paired component): $def_file")
          done < <(find overrides/app/components \
            -name "*ContentfulDefinition.ts" \
            ! -path "*/node_modules/*" 2>/dev/null | sort)

          COUNT=${#issues[@]}
          echo "count=$COUNT" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

          if [[ $COUNT -gt 0 ]]; then
            printf '%s\n' "${issues[@]}" > /tmp/contentful-issues.txt
            echo "has_issues=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          else
            echo "has_issues=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi

      - name: Report Contentful audit results
        if: steps.audit.outputs.has_issues == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          DATE=$(date +%Y-%m-%d)
          COUNT="${{ steps.audit.outputs.count }}"

          ITEMS=""
          while IFS= read -r issue; do
            ITEMS="${ITEMS}- [ ] ${issue}"$'\n'
          done < /tmp/contentful-issues.txt

          EXISTING=$(gh issue list \
            --label "contentful-drift" \
            --state open \
            --json number \
            --jq '.[0].number // empty')

          BODY=$(cat <<EOF
          ## Contentful Drift Audit — $DATE

          **$COUNT** structural issue(s) found in Contentful component definitions.

          ### Issues found

          $ITEMS

          ### Next steps

          Run \`/contentful-drift-check\` in a Claude Code session for a detailed
          prop-level comparison between component interfaces and their Contentful definitions.

          ---
          *Note: This automated check detects structural issues (orphaned files, missing pairs).*
          *Prop-level drift requires running \`/contentful-drift-check\` manually.*
          *Updated automatically by the weekly-agents workflow.*
          EOF
          )

          if [[ -n "$EXISTING" ]]; then
            gh issue edit "$EXISTING" \
              --title "Contentful drift audit: $COUNT issue(s) found ($DATE)" \
              --body "$BODY"
          else
            gh issue create \
              --title "Contentful drift audit: $COUNT issue(s) found ($DATE)" \
              --label "contentful-drift,needs-review" \
              --body "$BODY"
          fi

      - name: No Contentful drift issues
        if: steps.audit.outputs.has_issues == 'false'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          echo "✅ No structural Contentful definition issues found."
          EXISTING=$(gh issue list \
            --label "contentful-drift" \
            --state open \
            --json number \
            --jq '.[0].number // empty')
          if [[ -n "$EXISTING" ]]; then
            gh issue close "$EXISTING" \
              --comment "✅ No structural issues found this week. Closing automatically."
          fi

  changelog-reminder:
    name: Changelog reminder for open release PRs
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Check for open PRs targeting release branches without a changelog entry
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          # Find open PRs targeting release/**
          PRS=$(gh pr list \
            --base "release" \
            --state open \
            --json number,title,headRefName \
            --jq '.[] | "\(.number) \(.title)"' 2>/dev/null || true)

          if [[ -z "$PRS" ]]; then
            echo "No open PRs targeting release branches."
            exit 0
          fi

          while IFS= read -r pr; do
            PR_NUM=$(echo "$pr" | cut -d' ' -f1)
            # Check if the PR already has a changelog comment
            HAS_CHANGELOG=$(gh pr view "$PR_NUM" --json comments \
              --jq '[.comments[].body | select(contains("generate-changelog"))] | length')
            if [[ "$HAS_CHANGELOG" -eq 0 ]]; then
              gh pr comment "$PR_NUM" --body "$(cat <<EOF
          ### 📋 Changelog reminder

          This PR targets a release branch. Before merging, run:

          \`\`\`
          /generate-changelog
          \`\`\`

          This will produce audience-specific release notes for the dev team, QA, product, and GitHub Release.
          Commit the output to \`docs/releases/\` as part of this PR.
          EOF
          )"
            fi
          done <<< "$PRS"

name: Protected File Guard

# Server-side enforcement of the tier/squad model. The client-side
# .claude/hooks/tier2Warn.sh is non-blocking — this workflow is the
# authoritative gate at PR time.

on:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - develop
      - main
      - 'release/**'
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]

jobs:
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # JOB 1 — Warning (non-blocking): Tier 1 files touched.
  # NOT a required status check (see AGENTS.md > Tier 1 Approval for why).
  # The actual hard block is CODEOWNERS + require_code_owner_reviews on
  # branch protection, enforced natively by GitHub with no Actions
  # involvement. This job exists to post the loud, informative warning and
  # owner-contact-map — useful context, not the gate itself.
  #
  # History: this used to be a required check with a second job
  # (tier1-guard-recheck) that re-evaluated it on every review submission
  # via the Checks API, so it could flip from fail to pass without a new
  # commit. That approach stopped working once GitHub locked down check-run
  # updates to same-run-only in Feb 2025 (see
  # https://github.blog/changelog/2025-02-12-notice-of-upcoming-deprecations-and-breaking-changes-for-github-actions/#changes-to-check-run-status-modification) —
  # a different workflow run can no longer flip another run's check
  # conclusion. Since a single pull_request-triggered run can't wait around
  # for a future review, and re-running the whole job on review events just
  # creates a second, stale-vs-fresh check-run record under the same name
  # (which GitHub does NOT treat the newer one as superseding for
  # merge-blocking purposes), there's no way to make this job itself both
  # required and reliably self-updating. CODEOWNERS already does this
  # correctly and natively, so that's the real gate.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  tier1-guard:
    name: "🔴 Tier 1 — Frozen Files Check"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}

      - name: Get changed files
        id: changed
        uses: tj-actions/changed-files@2d756ea4c53f7f6b397767d8723b3a10a9f35bf2 # v44
        with:
          base_sha: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          sha: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          files_yaml: |
            tier1:
              # Design tokens — owner: UI Designer
              - 'overrides/app/theme/foundation/**'
              - 'overrides/app/theme/index.ts'
              # Commerce SDK hooks (overrides surface) — owner: Integration Lead
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-current-basket.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-current-customer.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-einstein.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-datacloud.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-refresh-token.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-multi-site.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-navigation.*'
              # Runtime & integration config — owner: Integration Lead
              - 'config/**'
              - 'overrides/app/ssr.*'
              - 'worker/main.*'
              - 'mobify.config.js'
              - 'package.json'
              - 'package-lock.json'
              # Test & tooling config — owner: Integration Lead
              - 'vitest.config.*'
              - 'playwright.config.*'
              - '.storybook/**'
              - 'tests/lighthouserc.*'
              - 'lighthouserc.*'
              # CI/CD — owner: Integration Lead
              - '.github/workflows/**'
              # Governance — owner: Both Squad Leads + Integration Lead
              - 'AGENTS.md'
              - 'CLAUDE.md'
              - 'CODEOWNERS'
              - '.claude/rules/**'
              - '.claude/settings.json'
              - 'coderabbit.yaml'
              - '.coderabbit/**'
              - 'semgrep.yml'
              - 'scripts/hooks/**'

      - name: Warn if Tier 1 files changed (informational — not a merge block)
        if: steps.changed.outputs.tier1_any_changed == 'true'
        run: |
          echo ""
          echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
          echo "🔴 TIER 1 PROTECTED FILES DETECTED IN THIS PR"
          echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
          echo ""
          echo "The following frozen files have been modified:"
          echo ""
          echo "${{ steps.changed.outputs.tier1_all_changed_files }}" | tr ' ' '\n' | sed 's/^/  ❌ /'
          echo ""
          echo "These files require an approving code-owner review before merge."
          echo "This check is informational — the actual merge block is CODEOWNERS +"
          echo "the required code-owner review, enforced by GitHub natively."
          echo ""
          echo "REQUIRED ACTIONS before this PR can be merged:"
          echo "  1. Get an approving review (not just a comment) from a member of"
          echo "     @ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers — CODEOWNERS auto-requests this."
          echo "  2. Contact the correct owner using the table below"
          echo ""
          echo "OWNER CONTACT MAP:"
          echo "  overrides/app/theme/foundation/      → UI Designer      (#design-system)"
          echo "  overrides/app/theme/index.ts         → UI Designer      (#design-system)"
          echo "  overrides/app/hooks/use-current-*   → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  overrides/app/hooks/use-einstein    → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  overrides/app/hooks/use-datacloud   → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  overrides/app/hooks/use-refresh-tok → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  overrides/app/hooks/use-multi-site  → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  overrides/app/hooks/use-navigation  → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  config/                             → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  overrides/app/ssr.*                 → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  worker/main.*                       → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  mobify.config.js                    → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  package.json (root)                 → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  vitest/playwright/.storybook config → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  .github/workflows/                  → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / CODEOWNERS  → Both Squad Leads + Integration Lead (#dev-team)"
          echo "  .claude/rules/ / .claude/settings   → Both Squad Leads + Integration Lead (#dev-team)"
          echo "  coderabbit.yaml / .coderabbit/      → Both Squad Leads + Integration Lead (#dev-team)"
          echo "  semgrep.yml / scripts/hooks/        → Both Squad Leads + Integration Lead (#dev-team)"
          echo ""
          echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"

      - name: Pass — no Tier 1 files changed
        if: steps.changed.outputs.tier1_any_changed == 'false'
        run: |
          echo "✅ No Tier 1 protected files detected in this PR."

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # JOB 2 — Hard block: PR targeting wrong branch
  # Prevents direct PRs to main that bypass develop
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  branch-target-guard:
    name: "🔴 Branch Target Check"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Block direct PRs to main from feature branches
        run: |
          BASE="${{ github.base_ref }}"
          HEAD="${{ github.head_ref }}"

          echo "Base branch: $BASE"
          echo "Head branch: $HEAD"

          # Feature branches must not go directly to main
          if [[ "$BASE" == "main" && "$HEAD" == feature/* ]]; then
            echo ""
            echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
            echo "🔴 INVALID BRANCH TARGET"
            echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
            echo ""
            echo "Feature branches must target 'develop', not 'main'."
            echo ""
            echo "Correct flow: feature/* → develop → (release/*) → main"
            echo ""
            echo "Please update the base branch of this PR to 'develop'."
            echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
            exit 1
          fi

          echo "✅ Branch target is valid."

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # JOB 3 — Warning (non-blocking): Tier 2 files touched
  # Posts a PR comment listing Tier 2 files and required reviewers
  # Does NOT fail the build — but CodeRabbit will escalate review
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  tier2-warning:
    name: "🟡 Tier 2 — Protected Files Warning"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Get changed Tier 2 files
        id: changed
        uses: tj-actions/changed-files@2d756ea4c53f7f6b397767d8723b3a10a9f35bf2 # v44
        with:
          files_yaml: |
            tier2:
              # Global shell — both squads
              - 'overrides/app/components/header/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/footer/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/drawer-menu/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/list-menu/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/seo/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/_app/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/_app-config/**'
              - 'overrides/app/routes.*'
              # Shared product components — Squad B primary, Squad A notified
              - 'overrides/app/components/product-tile/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/product-item/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/display-price/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/image-gallery/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/swatch-group/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/recommended-products/**'
              # Shared commerce components — Squad A primary, Squad B notified
              - 'overrides/app/components/order-summary/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/promo-code/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/pickup-or-delivery/**'
              # Theme component styles — UI Designer
              - 'overrides/app/theme/components/**'
              # Translations — Integration / SI Partner
              - 'translations/**'
              - 'overrides/app/static/translations/**'
              # Shared hooks — both squads
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-auth-modal.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-modal-state.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-intersection-observer.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-currency.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-dnt-notification.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-app-origin.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-selected-store.*'

      - name: Post Tier 2 warning comment on PR
        if: steps.changed.outputs.tier2_any_changed == 'true'
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const files = `${{ steps.changed.outputs.tier2_all_changed_files }}`
              .split(' ')
              .filter(Boolean)
              .map(f => `- \`${f}\``)
              .join('\n');

            const body = `## 🟡 Tier 2 Protected Files Detected

            This PR modifies shared components or hooks that are used across multiple features or squads.
            This is **not a merge block** — but it requires a second-developer review before merging.

            **Files affected:**
            ${files}

            **Required before merge:**
            - [ ] A developer from the **other squad** (not the PR author's squad) has reviewed and approved
            - [ ] The UI Designer has been notified if \`overrides/app/theme/components/\` is included
            - [ ] The Integration / SI Partner has been notified if \`translations/\` is included
            - [ ] No prop signature or export changes have been made without updating all consumers

            **Why this matters:** These files are imported by components in both Squad A and Squad B.
            A breaking change here — even a small one — will affect both squads simultaneously.

            _This comment is auto-generated by the Protected File Guard workflow._`;

            // Check if we already posted this comment to avoid duplicates
            const comments = await github.rest.issues.listComments({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
            });

            const existing = comments.data.find(c =>
              c.body.includes('Tier 2 Protected Files Detected') &&
              c.user.login === 'github-actions[bot]'
            );

            if (existing) {
              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                comment_id: existing.id,
                body,
              });
            } else {
              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                issue_number: context.issue.number,
                body,
              });
            }

      - name: Pass — no Tier 2 files changed
        if: steps.changed.outputs.tier2_any_changed == 'false'
        run: |
          echo "✅ No Tier 2 protected files detected in this PR."

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # JOB 4 — Cross-squad boundary detection
  # Warns when a PR touches both Squad A and Squad B territory
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  cross-squad-guard:
    name: "🟡 Cross-Squad Boundary Check"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Detect Squad A files changed
        id: squad-a
        uses: tj-actions/changed-files@2d756ea4c53f7f6b397767d8723b3a10a9f35bf2 # v44
        with:
          files_yaml: |
            squad_a:
              - 'overrides/app/pages/cart/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/checkout/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/checkout-one-click/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/confirmation/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/sf-payments-express/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/sf-payments-express-buttons/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/multiship/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/bonus-product-view-modal/**'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-checkout-auto-select.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-multiship.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-pickup-shipment.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-sf-payments.*'

      - name: Detect Squad B files changed
        id: squad-b
        uses: tj-actions/changed-files@2d756ea4c53f7f6b397767d8723b3a10a9f35bf2 # v44
        with:
          files_yaml: |
            squad_b:
              - 'overrides/app/pages/home/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/product-detail/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/product-list/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/search/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/account/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/wishlist/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/store-locator/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/search/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/store-locator/**'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-product-view-modal.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-derived-product.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-variant.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-wish-list.*'

      - name: Warn on cross-squad PR
        if: |
          steps.squad-a.outputs.squad_a_any_changed == 'true' &&
          steps.squad-b.outputs.squad_b_any_changed == 'true'
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const squadAFiles = `${{ steps.squad-a.outputs.squad_a_all_changed_files }}`
              .split(' ').filter(Boolean).map(f => `- \`${f}\``).join('\n');
            const squadBFiles = `${{ steps.squad-b.outputs.squad_b_all_changed_files }}`
              .split(' ').filter(Boolean).map(f => `- \`${f}\``).join('\n');

            const body = `## ⚠️ Cross-Squad Boundary Detected

            This PR modifies files owned by **both Squad A and Squad B**.
            This is unusual and should be intentional — not a side effect of an under-scoped Claude Code prompt.

            **Squad A files (Commerce & Checkout):**
            ${squadAFiles}

            **Squad B files (Discovery & Account):**
            ${squadBFiles}

            **Before merging, confirm:**
            - [ ] Both squad leads are aware this PR crosses squad boundaries
            - [ ] This is intentional and not the result of an over-broad code change
            - [ ] Both squad leads have approved this PR

            _This comment is auto-generated by the Protected File Guard workflow._`;

            const comments = await github.rest.issues.listComments({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
            });

            const existing = comments.data.find(c =>
              c.body.includes('Cross-Squad Boundary Detected') &&
              c.user.login === 'github-actions[bot]'
            );

            if (existing) {
              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                comment_id: existing.id,
                body,
              });
            } else {
              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                issue_number: context.issue.number,
                body,
              });
            }

name: Upstream Release Watch

# Opens a GitHub issue when @salesforce/retail-react-app ships a new release.
# This is an automated notifier — not a drift detector. See .docs/upstream-policy.md
# for what to do with the issue (usually: skim release notes, close, update
# .docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md).

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 0 * * 1'  # Every Monday at midnight UTC
  workflow_dispatch:      # Allow manual trigger for testing

permissions:
  issues: write
  contents: read

jobs:
  check-upstream-release:
    name: Check for new PWA Kit upstream release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Fetch latest upstream release tag
        id: upstream
        run: |
          RESPONSE=$(curl -sf \
            -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
            -H "X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28" \
            https://api.github.com/repos/SalesforceCommerceCloud/pwa-kit/releases/latest)
          LATEST_TAG=$(echo "$RESPONSE" | jq -r '.tag_name')
          RELEASE_URL=$(echo "$RESPONSE" | jq -r '.html_url')
          PUBLISHED_AT=$(echo "$RESPONSE" | jq -r '.published_at' | cut -c1-10)
          echo "tag=$LATEST_TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "url=$RELEASE_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "published=$PUBLISHED_AT" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Read baseline tag from upstreamBaseline.md
        id: baseline
        run: |
          BASELINE_TAG=$(grep -oP '(?<=<!-- upstream-release-tag: )[^\s]+(?= -->)' .docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md || echo "UNSET")
          echo "tag=$BASELINE_TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Check for existing open issue for this release
        id: existing
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          COUNT=$(gh issue list \
            --label "upstream-sync" \
            --state open \
            --json title \
            --jq '.[].title' \
            | grep -c "${{ steps.upstream.outputs.tag }}" || true)
          echo "count=$COUNT" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Open tracking issue
        if: |
          steps.upstream.outputs.tag != steps.baseline.outputs.tag &&
          steps.existing.outputs.count == '0'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          LATEST_TAG="${{ steps.upstream.outputs.tag }}"
          RELEASE_URL="${{ steps.upstream.outputs.url }}"
          PUBLISHED="${{ steps.upstream.outputs.published }}"
          BASELINE_TAG="${{ steps.baseline.outputs.tag }}"

          gh issue create \
            --title "Upstream release available: $LATEST_TAG" \
            --label "upstream-sync,needs-review" \
            --body "$(cat <<EOF
          ## New Salesforce PWA Kit release detected

          | | |
          |---|---|
          | New upstream release | [$LATEST_TAG]($RELEASE_URL) |
          | Published | $PUBLISHED |
          | Current baseline | $BASELINE_TAG |

          ---

          ## What to do

          Our policy is **bump opportunistically, not on a schedule.** See [.docs/upstream-policy.md](../blob/main/.docs/upstream-policy.md).

          1. Open the [release notes]($RELEASE_URL).
          2. Skim for:
             - **Security** — CVE fixes, dependency patches we are exposed to.
             - **SDK** — changes in \`pwa-kit-runtime\`, \`pwa-kit-react-sdk\`, \`commerce-sdk-react\`, or \`pwa-kit-dev\` that affect code we use.
             - **Bug fixes or features** we have been waiting for.
          3. **If nothing relevant:** close this issue with a one-line reason, and update \`Reviewed up to\` in [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](../blob/main/.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md). Do not bump.
          4. **If something relevant:** bump \`@salesforce/retail-react-app\` (and any related SDK packages), run \`npx tsc --noEmit\`, \`npm run build\`, \`npm run test\`, then update **both** \`Current\` and \`Reviewed up to\` (and the \`<!-- upstream-release-tag: ... -->\` marker) in upstreamBaseline.md.

          ---

          _Opened automatically by the upstream-release-watch workflow._
          EOF
          )"

      - name: Log no-op reason
        if: |
          steps.upstream.outputs.tag == steps.baseline.outputs.tag ||
          steps.existing.outputs.count != '0'
        run: |
          if [ "${{ steps.upstream.outputs.tag }}" = "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.tag }}" ]; then
            echo "No new release. Latest upstream (${{ steps.upstream.outputs.tag }}) matches current baseline."
          else
            echo "Issue already exists for ${{ steps.upstream.outputs.tag }}. No duplicate created."
          fi

name: SIT Gate

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - 'release/**'
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - 'release/**'

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write
  pages: write
  id-token: write

jobs:
  playwright-p0:
    name: Playwright P0 journeys
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: false
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        run: node_modules/.bin/playwright install --with-deps chromium

      - name: Run P0 suite
        run: node_modules/.bin/playwright test --project=p0 --reporter=html,github
        env:
          RETAIL_APP_HOME: ${{ vars.RETAIL_APP_HOME }}

      - name: Upload Playwright report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: playwright-report/
          retention-days: 30

      - name: Upload Pages artifact
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: playwright-report/

  deploy-playwright-report:
    name: Publish Playwright report to Pages
    needs: playwright-p0
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

  lighthouse-ci:
    name: Lighthouse CI
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: false
    env:
      LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL: ${{ secrets.LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL }}
      LHCI_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.LHCI_TOKEN }}
      LHCI_TARGET_URL: ${{ secrets.LHCI_TARGET_URL_SIT }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Run Lighthouse CI
        run: node_modules/.bin/lhci autorun

      - name: Upload Lighthouse results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: lighthouse-results
          path: .lighthouseci/
          retention-days: 30

  contract-tests:
    name: MuleSoft contract tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: false
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      # TODO: Replace with real contract assertion once MuleSoft publishes OpenAPI specs.
      # Owner: Zimmermann integration team + Accenture delivery lead to align.
      - name: Run contract tests
        run: npm run test:contracts

  bundle-size:
    name: Bundle size check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: false
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Build and check bundle size
        run: npm run test:max-file-size

  sit-gate:
    name: SIT Gate
    needs: [playwright-p0, lighthouse-ci, contract-tests, bundle-size]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Check all SIT signals passed
        run: |
          if [ "${{ needs.playwright-p0.result }}" != "success" ] || \
             [ "${{ needs.lighthouse-ci.result }}" != "success" ] || \
             [ "${{ needs.contract-tests.result }}" != "success" ] || \
             [ "${{ needs.bundle-size.result }}" != "success" ]; then
            echo "SIT gate: one or more checks failed"
            echo "  playwright-p0:   ${{ needs.playwright-p0.result }}"
            echo "  lighthouse-ci:   ${{ needs.lighthouse-ci.result }}"
            echo "  contract-tests:  ${{ needs.contract-tests.result }}"
            echo "  bundle-size:     ${{ needs.bundle-size.result }}"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "SIT gate: all checks passed"

    needs: dev-gate
    if: needs.dev-gate.result == 'success'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: dev
    env:
      MRT_USER: ${{ secrets.MRT_USER }}
      MRT_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.MRT_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Push build to dev
        run: npm run push:dev

  tag-sprint:
    name: Tag sprint rollover
    needs: dev-gate
    if: needs.dev-gate.result == 'success'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 2

      - name: Check for sprint.txt change
        id: sprint-check
        run: |
          if git diff HEAD~1 HEAD -- scripts/sprint.txt | grep -q .; then
            echo "changed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "sprint=$(cat scripts/sprint.txt | tr -d '[:space:]')" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "changed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Create sprint tag
        if: steps.sprint-check.outputs.changed == 'true'
        run: |
          SPRINT="${{ steps.sprint-check.outputs.sprint }}"
          TAG="sprint/${SPRINT}/$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)"
          git tag "$TAG"
          git push origin "$TAG"
          echo "Tagged: $TAG"

# CodeRabbit only runs Semgrep when this file exists in the repo root.
# Tested locally: python3 -m venv /tmp/semgrep-venv && /tmp/semgrep-venv/bin/pip install semgrep
#   /tmp/semgrep-venv/bin/semgrep scan --config semgrep.yml <file>
rules:
  - id: payment-credential-logged
    languages: [typescript]
    severity: ERROR
    message: >-
      Payment credential (card number, CVV, PIN) flows into a logging/telemetry sink.
      Per conventions.md, these must never appear in console.*, Sentry, or analytics calls.
    mode: taint
    pattern-sources:
      - pattern-either:
          - patterns:
              - pattern: function $FN(..., $VAR, ...) { ... }
              - metavariable-regex:
                  metavariable: $VAR
                  regex: (?i)(cardNumber|cvv|pin|cardNum|pan)
      - patterns:
          - pattern: const $VAR = ...
          - metavariable-regex:
              metavariable: $VAR
              regex: (?i)(cardNumber|cvv|pin|cardNum|pan)
    pattern-sinks:
      - pattern: console.$METHOD(...)
      - pattern: Sentry.$METHOD(...)

  - id: dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized
    languages: [typescript]
    severity: ERROR
    message: >-
      dangerouslySetInnerHTML used without an obvious sanitizer call (e.g. DOMPurify.sanitize) — XSS risk.
    patterns:
      - pattern: '<$TAG ... dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: $X }} ... />'
      - pattern-not: '<$TAG ... dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: $SANITIZER.sanitize(...) }} ... />'

1	<!-- synced-from: AGENTS.md, .claude/rules/conventions.md, .claude/rules/frozenFiles.md, .claude/rules/protectedFiles.md, .claude/rules/squadA.md, .claude/rules/squadB.md — edit the source(s), not this file, then run: node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix -->
2	
3	# Zimmermann PWA Kit — Copilot Instructions
4	
5	<!-- from: AGENTS.md -->
6	
7	# Zimmermann - Salesforce PWA Kit (Production)
8	
9	> **STRICT RULE — TypeScript only inside `overrides/`.**
10	> Every file created or modified under `overrides/` **must** use `.ts` or `.tsx`.
11	> `.js` and `.jsx` files are not acceptable here, including theme files, stories, and config modules.
12	> Run `npx tsc --noEmit` before finishing any task that touches `overrides/`.
13	
14	Production storefront for www.zimmermann.com, a luxury Australian fashion brand. Must be robust and secure and SEO-friendly. See [.docs/architecture.md](.docs/architecture.md) for stack overview, overrides pattern, component organisation, and key paths.
15	
16	Tier classifications and protected-file lists live in [.claude/rules/](.claude/rules/) — loaded automatically per session. Custom slash commands for scaffolding and review live in [.claude/skills/](.claude/skills/).
17	
18	## Branch Rules
19	
20	**At session start, always run `git branch --show-current`.** If the output is `develop` or `main`, stop immediately — do not make any changes.
21	
22	| Branch | Branched from | Merges to | Allowed? | Notes |
23	|---|---|---|---|---|
24	| `feature/*` | `develop` | `develop` | ✅ Yes | Primary working context for new work |
25	| `fix/*` | `develop` | `develop` | ✅ Yes | Non-urgent bug fixes. Mechanically identical to `feature/*` — naming is for commit hygiene |
26	| `release/*` | `develop` | `main` **and** `develop` | ⚠️ Supervised | Plan-first + confirm-every-edit required. Code logic fixes must use a `fix/release-*` sub-branch |
27	| `fix/release-{version}-*` | the `release/*` branch | the `release/*` branch, then forward-merged to `develop` once the release ships | ✅ Yes | Only path for code logic fixes on a release. PR targets the release branch; SIT gate runs against the PR. Treated like `feature/*` on the sub-branch itself — the "Supervised" plan-first + confirm-every-edit rules apply only to direct edits on the `release/*` branch |
28	| `hotfix/*` | `main` | `main` **and** `develop` | ✅ Yes | Urgent production fixes only. Tier 1 rules still apply. Must be back-merged to `develop` to prevent drift |
29	| `develop` | — | — | ❌ Never | Human commits only |
30	| `main` | — | — | ❌ Never | Human commits only |
31	
32	> **On `release/*` or `hotfix/*` branches you MUST read [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) before any action.** It holds the supervised-edit rules (plan-first, confirm-every-edit, `fix/release-*` sub-branch flow) and the GitFlow back-merge rules that apply in addition to the Hard Rules below. On `feature/*` and `fix/*`, ignore it.
33	
34	## Hard Rules
35	
36	1. **Never operate on `develop` or `main`** branches.
37	2. **Never modify a Tier 1 file** without the developer explicitly naming it in the prompt and confirming owner approval — unless the verified-session exception in [Tier 1 Approval](#tier-1-approval--how-its-actually-enforced) applies. See [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md).
38	3. **Never modify `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`** — all design token changes go through the UI designer.
39	4. **Never modify `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, or `worker/main.js`.** These are absolute — the verified-session exception in [Tier 1 Approval](#tier-1-approval--how-its-actually-enforced) does not apply to them, regardless of approver status. `.github/workflows/` is Tier 1 CI/CD config and instead follows the standard Hard Rule #2 process (verified-session exception applies).
40	5. **Never refactor upward.** Fixing a bug in a component does not mean touching the hook or utility it calls.
41	6. **Never rename or move a shared hook or component.**
42	7. **Never add or remove packages** from `package.json` without integration team approval. When approved, always use `npm install` rather than editing `package.json` directly.
43	8. **Never modify test configuration files** (`vitest.config.*`, `playwright.config.*`, `.storybook/`, `tests/lighthouserc.js`).
44	9. **Never delete files** without being explicitly asked in the current prompt. You may propose deletion and let a human confirm.
45	10. **Never touch more than one protection tier** in a single change without stopping to confirm scope with the developer.
46	11. **Never assume a hook is safe to modify** because it has a simple name — check the frozenFiles list first.
47	12. **When requirements are unclear, ask one clarifying question at a time.** Do not proceed with assumptions and do not batch questions. Wait for the answer before asking the next question or writing any code.

# Zimmermann - Salesforce PWA Kit (Production)

> **STRICT RULE — TypeScript only inside `overrides/`.**
> Every file created or modified under `overrides/` **must** use `.ts` or `.tsx`.
> `.js` and `.jsx` files are not acceptable here, including theme files, stories, and config modules.
> Run `npx tsc --noEmit` before finishing any task that touches `overrides/`.

Production storefront for www.zimmermann.com, a luxury Australian fashion brand. Must be robust and secure and SEO-friendly. See [.docs/architecture.md](.docs/architecture.md) for stack overview, overrides pattern, component organisation, and key paths.

Tier classifications and protected-file lists live in [.claude/rules/](.claude/rules/) — loaded automatically per session. Custom slash commands for scaffolding and review live in [.claude/skills/](.claude/skills/).

## Branch Rules

**At session start, always run `git branch --show-current`.** If the output is `develop` or `main`, stop immediately — do not make any changes.

| Branch | Branched from | Merges to | Allowed? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `feature/*` | `develop` | `develop` | ✅ Yes | Primary working context for new work |
| `fix/*` | `develop` | `develop` | ✅ Yes | Non-urgent bug fixes. Mechanically identical to `feature/*` — naming is for commit hygiene |
| `release/*` | `develop` | `main` **and** `develop` | ⚠️ Supervised | Plan-first + confirm-every-edit required. Code logic fixes must use a `fix/release-*` sub-branch |
| `fix/release-{version}-*` | the `release/*` branch | the `release/*` branch, then forward-merged to `develop` once the release ships | ✅ Yes | Only path for code logic fixes on a release. PR targets the release branch; SIT gate runs against the PR. Treated like `feature/*` on the sub-branch itself — the "Supervised" plan-first + confirm-every-edit rules apply only to direct edits on the `release/*` branch |
| `hotfix/*` | `main` | `main` **and** `develop` | ✅ Yes | Urgent production fixes only. Tier 1 rules still apply. Must be back-merged to `develop` to prevent drift |
| `develop` | — | — | ❌ Never | Human commits only |
| `main` | — | — | ❌ Never | Human commits only |

> **On `release/*` or `hotfix/*` branches you MUST read [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) before any action.** It holds the supervised-edit rules (plan-first, confirm-every-edit, `fix/release-*` sub-branch flow) and the GitFlow back-merge rules that apply in addition to the Hard Rules below. On `feature/*` and `fix/*`, ignore it.

## Hard Rules

1. **Never operate on `develop` or `main`** branches.
2. **Never modify a Tier 1 file** without the developer explicitly naming it in the prompt and confirming owner approval — unless the verified-session exception in [Tier 1 Approval](#tier-1-approval--how-its-actually-enforced) applies. 6. **Never rename or move a shared hook or component.**
7. **Never add or remove packages** from `package.json` without integration team approval. When approved, always use `npm install` rather than editing `package.json` directly.
