#!/bin/bash
# Pre-commit hook:
#   1. Regenerate the Claude Code registry and stage any changes.
#   2. Warn when staged components in components/ or ui/ have a paired
#      *ContentfulDefinition.ts that is not also staged.
#
# Install (run both — the commit-msg hook is a sibling that enforces conventional commits):
#   cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
#   cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Registry regeneration — keeps .claude/registry/ in sync with
#    overrides/app/{components,hooks,utils,pages}/ and routes.tsx/jsx.
#    Individually checked per location; skipped entirely (no node invocation
#    at all) when the commit doesn't touch any of them — e.g. a commit that
#    only touches config/ or tooling files. Stages any updated registry
#    files automatically.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only)

registry_components=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/components/' || true)
registry_hooks=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/hooks/' || true)
registry_utils=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/utils/' || true)
registry_pages=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/pages/' || true)
registry_routes=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/routes\.(tsx|jsx)$' || true)

if [ -n "$registry_components$registry_hooks$registry_utils$registry_pages$registry_routes" ] \
  && command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/generateRegistry.mjs" ]; then
  echo "Regenerating Claude Code registry..."
  node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs
  git add .claude/registry/
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1b. AI rules sync — when a .claude/ source file is staged, auto-regenerate
#     the derived files (.cursor/rules/, .vscode/instructions/,
#     .github/copilot-instructions.md) and stage the updates. Only the "auto"
#     targets are regenerated; manual targets remain untouched.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs" ]; then
  ai_sources_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
    | grep -E '^\.claude/(rules/.*\.md|skills/.*/SKILL\.md)$' \
    || true)

  if [ -n "$ai_sources_staged" ]; then
    echo "AI rule source(s) changed — running sync:ai-rules:fix..."
    node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix > /dev/null
    git add .cursor/rules/ .vscode/instructions/ .github/copilot-instructions.md 2>/dev/null || true
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1c. Skill inventory sync reminder — when a skill is added, removed, or
#     changed, remind the developer to update .claude/skills/README.md (the
#     canonical skill reference) and the mirrored Confluence page. Warning
#     only — there is no Confluence API integration wired up to verify this
#     automatically. Placed before the Contentful check's early exit (below)
#     so it always runs regardless of whether component files are staged.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

skill_files_staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
  | grep -E '^\.claude/skills/[^/]+/SKILL\.md$' \
  || true)

if [ -n "$skill_files_staged" ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "Skill file(s) changed:"
  echo "$skill_files_staged" | sed 's/^/  - /'

  if ! git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.claude/skills/README.md'; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ⚠️  .claude/skills/README.md is not staged — update it to match"
    echo "     (see 'Adding a new skill' at the bottom of that file)."
  fi

  echo ""
  echo "  ⚠️  Reminder: also update the mirrored Confluence page (child page under"
  echo "     page ID 297140226, \"Claude Code Skills Reference\") — there is no"
  echo "     automated push from this repo to Confluence yet."
  echo "  Committing anyway — this is a warning only."
  echo ""
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1d. .env.sample secret guard — BLOCKS the commit if a var whose name looks
#     like a secret (TOKEN/SECRET/KEY/PASSWORD/CREDENTIAL) has a non-empty
#     value staged in .env.sample. Real values belong only in .env (gitignored)
#     — see AGENTS.md > Rules > Environment variables. Checks the staged
#     (index) content, not the working tree, and runs before the Contentful
#     check's early exit below so it always executes.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.env.sample'; then
  leaked_vars=$(git show ':.env.sample' 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -E '^[A-Z0-9_]*(TOKEN|SECRET|KEY|PASSWORD|CREDENTIAL)[A-Z0-9_]*=.+$' \
    || true)

  if [ -n "$leaked_vars" ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — .env.sample contains non-empty secret-shaped value(s):"
    echo ""
    echo "$leaked_vars" | sed -E 's/=.*/=<redacted>/' | sed 's/^/       /'
    echo ""
    echo "  .env.sample must only ever contain blank placeholders for TOKEN/SECRET/KEY/"
    echo "  PASSWORD/CREDENTIAL variables (see AGENTS.md > Rules > Environment variables)."
    echo "  Move the real value(s) to your local .env (gitignored) and blank them here."
    echo ""
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Contentful definition drift check
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

WARNINGS=0

# Staged .jsx/.tsx files scoped to components/ or ui/ directories only
staged_components=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
  | grep -E '(components|ui)/.*\.(jsx|tsx)$' \
  | grep -v 'ContentfulDefinition' \
  || true)

[[ -z "$staged_components" ]] && exit 0

echo ""
echo "Checking for Contentful definition drift..."

while IFS= read -r file; do
  [[ -z "$file" ]] && continue

  dir=$(dirname "$file")
  base=$(basename "$file")
  base="${base%.*}"
  def_file="${dir}/${base}ContentfulDefinition.ts"

  # Only warn if a definition file exists
  [[ ! -f "$def_file" ]] && continue

  # Warn if the definition is not also staged alongside the component
  if ! git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF "$def_file"; then
    echo "  ⚠️  $(basename "$file") — definition not staged: $def_file"
    WARNINGS=$((WARNINGS + 1))
  fi
done <<< "$staged_components"

if [ "$WARNINGS" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "  $WARNINGS component(s) may have stale Contentful definitions."
  echo "  Run /contentful-drift-check to review, then stage any updated definition files."
  echo "  Committing anyway — this is a warning only."
  echo ""
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Derived configuration file guard
#    Blocks commits that directly edit derived files (.cursor/rules/,
#    .vscode/instructions/, .github/copilot-instructions.md) without also
#    staging the .claude/ source they were generated from.
#    Only triggers on MODIFIED files (diff-filter=M) — newly created derived
#    files are allowed through so the initial sync commit is not blocked.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

blocked_files=()

# Get all MODIFIED (not newly added) staged files
modified_staged=$(git diff --cached --diff-filter=M --name-only || true)

while IFS= read -r file; do
  [[ -z "$file" ]] && continue

  # Only check files in derived locations
  case "$file" in
    .cursor/rules/*|.vscode/instructions/*|.github/copilot-instructions.md) ;;
    *) continue ;;
  esac

  # Only check if the file exists and contains a synced-from comment
  [[ ! -f "$file" ]] && continue
  synced_line=$(grep -m1 'synced-from:' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [[ -z "$synced_line" ]] && continue

  # Extract the first source path from the synced-from comment
  # Format: <!-- synced-from: path/to/source.md[, path2] — ... -->
  # or:     <!-- synced-from: path/to/source.md — ... -->
  synced_from=$(echo "$synced_line" \
    | sed 's/.*synced-from:[[:space:]]*//' \
    | sed 's/[[:space:]]*—.*//' \
    | sed 's/,.*//' \
    | tr -d ' ')

  [[ -z "$synced_from" ]] && continue

  # If the source is also staged in this commit, this is a legitimate sync
  # update — the developer edited the .claude/ source and ran the sync script.
  # Skip it.
  if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF "$synced_from"; then
    continue
  fi

  # Source is NOT staged — this derived file was edited directly.
  blocked_files+=("$file")

done <<< "$modified_staged"

if [ "${#blocked_files[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — derived configuration file(s) edited directly:"
  echo ""
  for bf in "${blocked_files[@]}"; do
    echo "       $bf"
  done
  echo ""
  echo "  These files are generated from .claude/ sources and must not be edited directly."
  echo ""
  echo "  To update auto-generated rules:"
  echo "    1. Edit the .claude/ source (see the synced-from comment at the top of the file)"
  echo "    2. Run: node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix"
  echo "    3. Commit the .claude/ source and the regenerated file together"
  echo ""
  echo "  To propose changes to .claude/ master files or sync rules:"
  echo "    Raise the request to the Tech Lead via #dev-team"
  echo ""
  exit 1
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. .env.sample secrets guard
#    Blocks commits where a secret-class key has a non-empty value, or where
#    a value matches a known credential pattern (JWT, long hex, base64, provider
#    prefixes). Runs only when .env.sample is staged.
#    Secret-class key names: *_SECRET, *_TOKEN, *_PASSWORD, *_CREDENTIAL,
#    *_PRIVATE_KEY, *_API_KEY, *_BEARER, *_SIGNING_KEY, *_ENCRYPTION_KEY,
#    *_DSN, *_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
#    Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, SHORT_CODE, CLIENT_ID,
#    SPACE_ID, ENVIRONMENT_ID, OCAPI_HOST) may keep placeholder values.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.env.sample'; then
  secret_violations=()

  while IFS= read -r line; do
    [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] && continue
    [[ -z "${line// }" ]] && continue
    [[ "$line" =~ ^([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$ ]] || continue
    key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
    value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
    [[ -z "$value" ]] && continue

    # Secret-class key name with a non-empty value
    if echo "$key" | grep -qE '(_SECRET|_TOKEN|_PASSWORD|_CREDENTIAL|_PRIVATE_KEY|_API_KEY|_BEARER|_SIGNING_KEY|_ENCRYPTION_KEY|_DSN|_WEBHOOK_SECRET)'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (secret-class key name with non-empty value)")
      continue
    fi

    # Value looks like a JWT
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a JWT)")
      continue
    fi

    # Value looks like a hex credential (32+ pure hex chars)
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[0-9a-fA-F]{32,}$'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a hex credential)")
      continue
    fi

    # Value looks like a base64 credential (40+ chars)
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9+/]{40,}={0,2}$'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a base64 credential)")
      continue
    fi

    # Known provider-specific key prefixes
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^(AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|ghs_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{32,}|xox[bpars]-[A-Za-z0-9-]+)'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value matches a known provider secret format)")
      continue
    fi

  done < <(git show ":0:.env.sample" 2>/dev/null || true)

  if [ "${#secret_violations[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — .env.sample contains secret-class key(s) with non-empty values:"
    echo ""
    for v in "${secret_violations[@]}"; do
      echo "    $v"
    done
    echo ""
    echo "  .env.sample must only contain blank values for secret-class keys."
    echo "  Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, etc.) may keep their values."
    echo ""
    echo "  Remove the value(s) above, re-stage .env.sample, and commit again."
    echo ""
    exit 1
  fi
fi

exit 0
#!/bin/bash
# commit-msg: enforces conventional commits format on every commit.
#
# Install: cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg
#          chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg

commit_msg=$(cat "$1")

# Pass through merge commits, reverts, fixups, and WIP
if echo "$commit_msg" | grep -qE '^(Merge|Revert|fixup!|squash!|WIP)'; then
  exit 0
fi

# Conventional commits pattern
# type(optional-scope): description
# upstream-sync is a Zimmermann-specific type for PWA Kit sync changes
pattern='^(feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|build|ci|chore|upstream-sync)(\([a-z0-9/._-]+\))?: .{1,100}$'

if ! echo "$commit_msg" | grep -qE "$pattern"; then
  echo ""
  echo "  ❌  Commit rejected — message does not follow conventional commits format."
  echo ""
  echo "  Required:  type(scope): short description"
  echo ""
  echo "  Types:"
  echo "    feat           new feature"
  echo "    fix            bug fix"
  echo "    docs           documentation only"
  echo "    style          formatting, no logic change"
  echo "    refactor       neither fix nor feat"
  echo "    perf           performance improvement"
  echo "    test           adding or updating tests"
  echo "    build          build system or dependency changes"
  echo "    ci             CI/CD configuration"
  echo "    chore          maintenance tasks"
  echo "    upstream-sync  upstream Salesforce PWA Kit sync"
  echo ""
  echo "  Scope examples (optional but encouraged):"
  echo "    product-tile  checkout  auth  header  search"
  echo "    global-e  adyen  contentful  searchspring"
  echo "    pwa-kit-runtime  commerce-sdk-react"
  echo ""
  echo "  Examples:"
  echo "    feat(product-tile): add sale badge for discounted variants"
  echo "    fix(checkout): resolve shipping method not persisting on refresh"
  echo "    upstream-sync(pwa-kit-runtime): apply v3.18.0 SSR cache fix"
  echo "    chore(deps): update @salesforce/commerce-sdk-react to 5.3.0"
  echo "    test(use-current-basket): add guest basket merge coverage"
  echo ""
  exit 1
fi

exit 0

  if [ -n "$leaked_vars" ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — .env.sample contains non-empty secret-shaped value(s):"
    echo ""
    echo "$leaked_vars" | sed -E 's/=.*/=<redacted>/' | sed 's/^/       /'
    echo ""
    echo "  .env.sample must only ever contain blank placeholders for TOKEN/SECRET/KEY/"
    echo "  PASSWORD/CREDENTIAL variables (see AGENTS.md > Rules > Environment variables)."
    echo "  Move the real value(s) to your local .env (gitignored) and blank them here."
    echo ""
    exit 1
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Contentful definition drift check
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

WARNINGS=0

# Staged .jsx/.tsx files scoped to components/ or ui/ directories only
staged_components=$(git diff --cached --name-only \
  | grep -E '(components|ui)/.*\.(jsx|tsx)$' \
  | grep -v 'ContentfulDefinition' \
  || true)

[[ -z "$staged_components" ]] && exit 0

echo ""
echo "Checking for Contentful definition drift..."

while IFS= read -r file; do
  [[ -z "$file" ]] && continue

  dir=$(dirname "$file")
  base=$(basename "$file")
  base="${base%.*}"
  def_file="${dir}/${base}ContentfulDefinition.ts"

  # Only warn if a definition file exists
  [[ ! -f "$def_file" ]] && continue

  # Warn if the definition is not also staged alongside the component
  if ! git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF "$def_file"; then
    echo "  ⚠️  $(basename "$file") — definition not staged: $def_file"
    WARNINGS=$((WARNINGS + 1))
  fi
done <<< "$staged_components"

if [ "$WARNINGS" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "  $WARNINGS component(s) may have stale Contentful definitions."
  echo "  Run /contentful-drift-check to review, then stage any updated definition files."
  echo "  Committing anyway — this is a warning only."
  echo ""
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Derived configuration file guard
#    Blocks commits that directly edit derived files (.cursor/rules/,
#    .vscode/instructions/, .github/copilot-instructions.md) without also
#    staging the .claude/ source they were generated from.
#    Only triggers on MODIFIED files (diff-filter=M) — newly created derived
#    files are allowed through so the initial sync commit is not blocked.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

blocked_files=()

# Get all MODIFIED (not newly added) staged files
modified_staged=$(git diff --cached --diff-filter=M --name-only || true)

while IFS= read -r file; do
  [[ -z "$file" ]] && continue

  # Only check files in derived locations
  case "$file" in
    .cursor/rules/*|.vscode/instructions/*|.github/copilot-instructions.md) ;;
    *) continue ;;
  esac

  # Only check if the file exists and contains a synced-from comment
  [[ ! -f "$file" ]] && continue
  synced_line=$(grep -m1 'synced-from:' "$file" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [[ -z "$synced_line" ]] && continue

  # Extract the first source path from the synced-from comment
  # Format: <!-- synced-from: path/to/source.md[, path2] — ... -->
  # or:     <!-- synced-from: path/to/source.md — ... -->
  synced_from=$(echo "$synced_line" \
    | sed 's/.*synced-from:[[:space:]]*//' \
    | sed 's/[[:space:]]*—.*//' \
    | sed 's/,.*//' \
    | tr -d ' ')

  [[ -z "$synced_from" ]] && continue

  # If the source is also staged in this commit, this is a legitimate sync
  # update — the developer edited the .claude/ source and ran the sync script.
  # Skip it.
  if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF "$synced_from"; then
    continue
  fi

  # Source is NOT staged — this derived file was edited directly.
  blocked_files+=("$file")

done <<< "$modified_staged"

if [ "${#blocked_files[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo ""
  echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — derived configuration file(s) edited directly:"
  echo ""
  for bf in "${blocked_files[@]}"; do
    echo "       $bf"
  done
  echo ""
  echo "  These files are generated from .claude/ sources and must not be edited directly."
  echo ""
  echo "  To update auto-generated rules:"
  echo "    1. Edit the .claude/ source (see the synced-from comment at the top of the file)"
  echo "    2. Run: node scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs --fix"
  echo "    3. Commit the .claude/ source and the regenerated file together"
  echo ""
  echo "  To propose changes to .claude/ master files or sync rules:"
  echo "    Raise the request to the Tech Lead via #dev-team"
  echo ""
  exit 1
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. .env.sample secrets guard
#    Blocks commits where a secret-class key has a non-empty value, or where
#    a value matches a known credential pattern (JWT, long hex, base64, provider
#    prefixes). Runs only when .env.sample is staged.
#    Secret-class key names: *_SECRET, *_TOKEN, *_PASSWORD, *_CREDENTIAL,
#    *_PRIVATE_KEY, *_API_KEY, *_BEARER, *_SIGNING_KEY, *_ENCRYPTION_KEY,
#    *_DSN, *_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
#    Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, SHORT_CODE, CLIENT_ID,
#    SPACE_ID, ENVIRONMENT_ID, OCAPI_HOST) may keep placeholder values.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -qF '.env.sample'; then
  secret_violations=()

  while IFS= read -r line; do
    [[ "$line" =~ ^[[:space:]]*# ]] && continue
    [[ -z "${line// }" ]] && continue
    [[ "$line" =~ ^([A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*)=(.*)$ ]] || continue
    key="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
    value="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
    [[ -z "$value" ]] && continue

    # Secret-class key name with a non-empty value
    if echo "$key" | grep -qE '(_SECRET|_TOKEN|_PASSWORD|_CREDENTIAL|_PRIVATE_KEY|_API_KEY|_BEARER|_SIGNING_KEY|_ENCRYPTION_KEY|_DSN|_WEBHOOK_SECRET)'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (secret-class key name with non-empty value)")
      continue
    fi

    # Value looks like a JWT
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a JWT)")
      continue
    fi

    # Value looks like a hex credential (32+ pure hex chars)
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[0-9a-fA-F]{32,}$'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a hex credential)")
      continue
    fi

    # Value looks like a base64 credential (40+ chars)
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9+/]{40,}={0,2}$'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value looks like a base64 credential)")
      continue
    fi

    # Known provider-specific key prefixes
    if echo "$value" | grep -qE '^(AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|ghs_[A-Za-z0-9]{36}|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{32,}|xox[bpars]-[A-Za-z0-9-]+)'; then
      secret_violations+=("  $key  (value matches a known provider secret format)")
      continue
    fi

  done < <(git show ":0:.env.sample" 2>/dev/null || true)

  if [ "${#secret_violations[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo ""
    echo "  ❌  Commit blocked — .env.sample contains secret-class key(s) with non-empty values:"
    echo ""
    for v in "${secret_violations[@]}"; do
      echo "    $v"
    done
    echo ""
    echo "  .env.sample must only contain blank values for secret-class keys."
    echo "  Non-secret public identifiers (ORG_ID, SITE_ID, etc.) may keep their values."
    echo ""
    echo "  Remove the value(s) above, re-stage .env.sample, and commit again."
    echo ""
    exit 1
  fi
fi

exit 0
#!/bin/bash
# commit-msg: enforces conventional commits format on every commit.
#
# Install: cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg
#          chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg

commit_msg=$(cat "$1")

# Pass through merge commits, reverts, fixups, and WIP
if echo "$commit_msg" | grep -qE '^(Merge|Revert|fixup!|squash!|WIP)'; then
  exit 0
fi

# Conventional commits pattern
# type(optional-scope): description
# upstream-sync is a Zimmermann-specific type for PWA Kit sync changes
pattern='^(feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|build|ci|chore|upstream-sync)(\([a-z0-9/._-]+\))?: .{1,100}$'

if ! echo "$commit_msg" | grep -qE "$pattern"; then
  echo ""
  echo "  ❌  Commit rejected — message does not follow conventional commits format."
  echo ""
  echo "  Required:  type(scope): short description"
  echo ""
  echo "  Types:"
  echo "    feat           new feature"
  echo "    fix            bug fix"
  echo "    docs           documentation only"
  echo "    style          formatting, no logic change"
  echo "    refactor       neither fix nor feat"
  echo "    perf           performance improvement"
  echo "    test           adding or updating tests"
  echo "    build          build system or dependency changes"
  echo "    ci             CI/CD configuration"
  echo "    chore          maintenance tasks"
  echo "    upstream-sync  upstream Salesforce PWA Kit sync"
  echo ""
  echo "  Scope examples (optional but encouraged):"
  echo "    product-tile  checkout  auth  header  search"
  echo "    global-e  adyen  contentful  searchspring"
  echo "    pwa-kit-runtime  commerce-sdk-react"
  echo ""
  echo "  Examples:"
  echo "    feat(product-tile): add sale badge for discounted variants"
  echo "    fix(checkout): resolve shipping method not persisting on refresh"
  echo "    upstream-sync(pwa-kit-runtime): apply v3.18.0 SSR cache fix"
  echo "    chore(deps): update @salesforce/commerce-sdk-react to 5.3.0"
  echo "    test(use-current-basket): add guest basket merge coverage"
  echo ""
  exit 1
fi

exit 0

name: Deploy SIT

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['SIT Gate']
    types:
      - completed
    branches:
      - 'release/**'

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

jobs:
  deploy-sit:
    name: Deploy to SIT
    if: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: sit
    env:
      MRT_USER: ${{ secrets.MRT_USER }}
      MRT_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.MRT_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Push build to SIT
        run: npm run push:sit

name: Deploy UAT

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      ref:
        description: 'Branch or tag to deploy (e.g. release/1.2.0)'
        required: true
        default: 'develop'

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

jobs:
  deploy-uat:
    name: Deploy to UAT
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: uat
    env:
      MRT_USER: ${{ secrets.MRT_USER }}
      MRT_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.MRT_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.ref }}

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Push build to UAT
        run: npm run push:uat

Here is the full map of every automated, AI-driven, and human-in-the-loop review mechanism in this codebase. --- ## Zimmermann PWA — Automated and AI Review Workflow Map --- ### 1. Claude Code Configuration (`.claude/`) #### `.claude/settings.json` The core Claude Code harness configuration. Three types of hooks fire on every session: **PreToolUse — fires before any file write or edit:** - Branch guard: blocks all file changes if the current branch is `develop` or `main` (hard exit 1). - Tier 2 warn hook (`tier2Warn.sh`): emits a non-blocking owner warning before editing any protected shared component, hook, or translation file. **PostToolUse — fires after writes/edits:** - Auto-Prettier: after every `Write` operation, runs Prettier on the new file via the project's local binary. - Contentful drift warn (`contentfulDriftWarn.sh`): after any component `.tsx` edit, checks whether a paired `*ContentfulDefinition.ts` exists and reminds the developer to run `/contentful-drift-check`. - Registry update (`registryUpdate.sh`): after any edit under `overrides/app/components|hooks|utils|pages` or `routes.tsx`, re-runs `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` to keep `.claude/registry/` in sync. - Test file reminder (`testFileRemind.sh`): after writing a new component or hook source file, warns if no `.test.*` file exists alongside it. **Stop hook:** - Session reflect (`session-reflect.sh`): at the end of every session that produced file changes, prompts Claude to draft a documentation proposal file under `.docs/agents-proposals/`. It never edits `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.docs/memory/`, or `.claude/rules/` directly — only proposes. **Permission allowlist** (in `settings.json`): pre-approves read-only Bash operations (`git branch`, `git status`, `git diff`, `git log`, `git show`, `find`, `grep`, `ls`) and the three run commands (`npm run lint`, `npm run test`, `npm run build`). #### `.claude/settings.local.json` Adds local machine-specific permissions (MCP Atlassian access) and enables all project MCP servers. Not committed to the shared settings. #### `CLAUDE.md` (Tier 1 governance file) The primary instruction document for Claude Code. References `AGENTS.md` via `@AGENTS.md`. Establishes 15 Hard Rules including: never operate on `develop`/`main`, never modify Tier 1 files without verified owner identity check (`gh api` against `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`), TypeScript-only rule, never add packages without approval, never create commits without explicit request. #### `AGENTS.md` The main AI agent instructions document (also consumed by GitHub Copilot and Cursor via `syncCursorRules.mjs`). Covers branch rules, coding task workflow (4-step: clarify → plan → copy-first → implement), "when to stop and ask a human" table, testing layers, performance requirements, and living memory conventions. #### `.claude/rules/` (6 files, all Tier 1) Rules loaded automatically per session: - `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/rules/conventions.md` — cross-cutting naming, import, DRY/KISS/SOLID, security rules - `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/rules/typescript.md` — TypeScript idioms (no `any`, `type` vs `interface`, `readonly`, etc.) - `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/rules/css.md` — Chakra token usage, no hardcoded design values, `.scss` conventions - `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/rules/components.md` — component/hook structure, Storybook categorisation, composition rules, accessibility enforcement (which is mechanically backed by ast-grep rules) - `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/rules/testing.md` — three-layer test strategy (Vitest/Storybook play/Playwright), file layout, mocking policy, gherkin-first QA workflow - `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` — Tier 1 frozen file list - `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` — Tier 2 protected file list #### `.claude/registry/` (5 markdown files) Auto-generated index of all components, hooks, utils, pages, and routes under `overrides/app/`. Updated on every commit via the pre-commit hook and on every file edit via the PostToolUse `registryUpdate.sh` hook. Used by `/feature-spec` and `/code-quality` skills to find relevant existing assets without brute-force filesystem scans. #### `.claude/skills/` (14 skills, each a `SKILL.md`) These are structured, human-in-the-lead workflows invoked as slash commands. All review-related ones: | Skill | Path | What it does | |---|---|---| | `/session-start` | `.claude/skills/session-start/SKILL.md` | Mandatory start-of-session ritual: branch check, reads `.docs/memory/` tracking docs, health checks, states position | | `/feature-spec` | `.claude/skills/feature-spec/SKILL.md` | Turns plain-English feature request into scoped spec (no code). Asks clarifying questions one at a time, spawns 3 parallel research agents, checks sprint scope | | `/scope-check` | `.claude/skills/scope-check/SKILL.md` | Reviews a proposed prompt before running it — classifies files by tier, detects drift risk, verdicts SAFE/RISKY/BLOCKED | | `/audit-tier` | `.claude/skills/audit-tier/SKILL.md` | Identifies protection tier, owner, and blast radius for any path | | `/code-quality` | `.claude/skills/code-quality/SKILL.md` | Read-only audit of changed files against all `.claude/rules/` — for large diffs spawns 4 parallel sub-agents (naming, imports, TypeScript, test coverage) | | `/pr-checklist` | `.claude/skills/pr-checklist/SKILL.md` | Runs `/code-quality`, classifies files by tier, generates copy-paste PR description with test/reviewer checklist | | `/qa-generate` | `.claude/skills/qa-generate/SKILL.md` | Two-phase E2E test generation: drafts Gherkin `.feature`, hard-stops until Lead QA approves, then generates Playwright spec | | `/contentful-drift-check` | `.claude/skills/contentful-drift-check/SKILL.md` | Read-only prop-vs-definition comparison for all Contentful-registered components | | `/upstream-sync-review` | `.claude/skills/upstream-sync-review/SKILL.md` | Reviews upstream PWA Kit release notes, maps to override surface, recommends BUMP/DEFER | | `/generate-changelog` | `.claude/skills/generate-changelog/SKILL.md` | Produces 4-audience changelog from conventional commits | --- ### 2. CI/CD Pipelines (`.github/workflows/`) #### `qa.yml` — triggers on every PR to `develop` or `release/**` The main quality gate for feature PRs. Human-in-the-Loop Responsibilities (What the Automation Does Not Cover) Based on the full picture above, these are the deliberate human gates: **Approval and merge decisions:** - Tier 1 file changes require a human member of `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` to submit an approving code-owner review (enforced by GitHub branch protection — cannot be bypassed by any automation) - Tier 2 file changes require a second developer (not the PR author) to review before merge - Cross-squad PRs require both squad leads to approve **QA workflow:** - Lead QA must validate the Gherkin `.feature` file before any Playwright spec is generated (`/qa-generate` hard-stops and waits for explicit confirmation) - Lead QA must annotate corrections with `# QA ANNOTATION:` comments; Playwright spec is not generated until sign-off - Manual screen-reader and keyboard-only navigation testing before marking accessibility checklist complete - UAT and STG deployments are manually triggered (`workflow_dispatch` only) - Production deployment is manually triggered **Requirement and scope decisions:** - Ambiguous or missing requirements must be resolved by a human before Claude writes any code (Hard Rule #12) - Shared hook function signature changes require a team RFC - New package dependencies require Integration team approval - Changes affecting more than one regional site config require Integration team sign-off - Sprint scope decisions (what belongs in a later sprint) are human-curated in `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` - Contentful prop-level drift resolution (the automated check detects it; a human decides how to fix it) **Documentation and governance updates:** - `session-reflect.sh` proposes doc changes but writes only to `.docs/agents-proposals/` — a human must review and apply any updates to `AGENTS.md`, `.docs/memory/`, `.claude/rules/`, or PRDs
